title: Omnivae — Engineering and Agent Rules
text:
# Omnivae — Engineering and Agent Rules

> Status: Binding rules for AGY/coding agents  
> Version: 1.0  
> Last consolidated: 2026-09-08

title: 0. Purpose
text:
## 0. Purpose

This document tells an implementation agent **how to work on Omnivae without corrupting the product intent, architecture, security model, or progress state**.

These rules are not suggestions. When a rule conflicts with convenience, convenience loses unless the product owner explicitly changes the rule.

---

title: 1. Source-of-truth precedence
text:
## 1. Source-of-truth precedence

When information conflicts, use this precedence:

1. **Latest explicit instruction from the product owner in the active work session.**
2. **`rules.md`** for non-negotiable process/security/completion behavior.
3. **`prd.md`** for required product behavior.
4. **`architecture.md`** for technical boundaries and flows.
5. **`schema.md`** for data contracts.
6. **`testing.md`** for verification and completion gates.
7. **`phases.md`** for planned sequencing.
8. **`memory.md`** for current state, recent implementation decisions, blockers, and working context.

If a lower-priority document contains a newer implementation fact that legitimately supersedes a higher-level assumption, do not silently reconcile it. Record the conflict in `memory.md` and update the relevant source document or ADR.

---

title: 2. Product identity rules
text:
## 2. Product identity rules

- The product name is **Omnivae**.
- Do not rename it in code, docs, UI, package metadata, or examples unless explicitly instructed.
- Old references such as LifeOS are historical context only and should be migrated when touching relevant files.
- Position Omnivae as a **personal intelligence / life orchestration system**, not only a planner or habit tracker.
- Job/Career is optional and must never be a mandatory onboarding assumption.

---

title: 3. Core invariants
text:
## 3. Core invariants

Never violate these invariants:

1. Local-first.
2. Privacy-first.
3. Offline-capable core workflows.
4. Multiple profiles are isolated.
5. Optional modules are truly optional.
6. User controls AI data access and consequential AI writes.
7. AI chat/memory are local by default.
8. BYOK secrets are securely stored and never logged.
9. Domain logic is independent of IndexedDB/SQLite/cloud vendors.
10. Daily/weekly/monthly/yearly progress derives from the same underlying records.
11. Health data is permissioned and handled more conservatively than ordinary UI metadata.
12. AI-generated claims do not become factual progress without evidence or user confirmation.
13. A feature is not complete until all required tests pass.

---

title: 4. Completion rule — absolute
text:
## 4. Completion rule — absolute

**NEVER mark a task, subtask, feature, issue, milestone, phase, migration, refactor, or bug fix as `complete`, `done`, `passed`, or equivalent until every test case required by `testing.md` for that scope has passed.**

This includes work that appears visually correct.

Allowed states before tests pass:

- `not_started`
- `in_progress`
- `implemented_unverified`
- `blocked`
- `failed_tests`
- `ready_for_verification`

Only after required test evidence exists:

- `completed`

If one required test fails, the scope remains incomplete.

If a test cannot run because infrastructure is missing, the scope remains incomplete and is marked `blocked` or `implemented_unverified`.

Do not weaken, skip, delete, quarantine, or rewrite a legitimate failing test merely to mark a feature complete.

---

title: 5. Required work cycle for every implementation task
text:
## 5. Required work cycle for every implementation task

Use this cycle:

```text
1. Read relevant docs
2. Inspect current code/tests/schema
3. Restate task internally as acceptance criteria
4. Identify impacted modules/data/security/offline behavior
5. Add or update tests
6. Implement minimal correct change
7. Run focused tests
8. Run required regression suites
9. Fix failures
10. Update docs/memory/migrations
11. Record test evidence
12. Only then mark complete
```

For a bug:

```text
reproduce → failing regression test → fix → regression passes → broader required tests → complete
```

---

title: 6. Before writing code
text:
## 6. Before writing code

An agent must inspect:

- the relevant section of `prd.md`,
- relevant architecture boundaries,
- relevant schema entities/migrations,
- required tests,
- `memory.md` for active work/blockers.

Do not implement from a ticket title alone.

Before changing an architectural boundary, inspect `architecture.md` and create/update an ADR or explicit decision record.

---

title: 7. Scope discipline
text: ## 7. Scope discipline

title: Do
text:
### Do

- make the smallest coherent change that fully satisfies acceptance criteria,
- preserve existing public contracts unless migration is intentional,
- refactor only where needed for correctness/maintainability,
- leave unrelated modules untouched,
- document unavoidable follow-up work.

title: Do not
text:
### Do not

- rewrite the whole app because a local change is inconvenient,
- introduce a new framework for one feature without justification,
- add speculative infrastructure,
- broaden feature scope silently,
- implement future P3 behavior inside a P0 task unless it is a necessary seam/interface.

---

title: 8. Architecture-change rule
text:
## 8. Architecture-change rule

An architectural change includes, but is not limited to:

- replacing Next.js/React,
- replacing Capacitor strategy,
- replacing the storage abstraction,
- making cloud mandatory,
- adding microservices,
- changing profile ownership model,
- changing sync identity/version semantics,
- changing encryption/key hierarchy,
- allowing autonomous agent writes,
- changing primary data store shape substantially.

For such changes:

1. Do not silently implement.
2. Add an ADR/decision note.
3. State motivation, alternatives, consequences, migration impact, testing impact.
4. Update `architecture.md`, `schema.md`, `phases.md`, and `memory.md` as applicable.

---

title: 9. Data ownership and profile isolation rules
text:
## 9. Data ownership and profile isolation rules

Every personal record must have an enforceable profile ownership path.

title: Required
text:
### Required

- repository calls are profile-scoped,
- queries include profile constraints,
- cross-profile IDs return not-found/forbidden safely,
- exports include only the active/selected profile,
- AI retrieval never crosses profiles,
- file attachments never cross profiles,
- caches/projections are profile-scoped,
- test fixtures include at least two profiles for isolation tests.

title: Forbidden
text:
### Forbidden

- global `getAllTasks()` over every profile for ordinary product use,
- client-controlled owner reassignment without validation,
- using display name as ownership key,
- using only UI filtering as security.

---

title: 10. Local-first rules
text:
## 10. Local-first rules

A feature belongs in the core only if its primary CRUD/read experience can function locally unless the feature is inherently external.

Examples:

- Task CRUD: local.
- Notes: local.
- Calendar local events: local.
- Journal: local.
- Dashboard: local.
- Health imported history after import: locally viewable.
- Hosted AI generation: network-dependent, but existing chat/history remains locally viewable.
- External calendar sync: network-dependent; local events still work.

When offline:

- never discard user input,
- do not show generic success for a network action that did not happen,
- label queued/pending/failed external actions,
- keep local data consistent.

---

title: 11. Storage rules
text:
## 11. Storage rules

- Domain/application code must depend on repository/storage ports.
- UI components must not own persistence logic.
- IndexedDB/SQLite details remain in adapters.
- Use stable IDs suitable for future sync.
- Every schema change requires a migration/version update.
- Migrations require tests.
- Avoid storing large blobs inline in relational/domain records when a file/blob abstraction is appropriate.
- Derived aggregates must be rebuildable.
- Deletions intended for future sync should have explicit tombstone semantics where required.

Do not use browser `localStorage` as the main structured database.

---

title: 12. Time and date rules
text:
## 12. Time and date rules

- Store absolute instants robustly, normally UTC.
- Preserve IANA timezone for timezone-bound schedules.
- All-day/local-day records need explicit local-date semantics.
- Recurrence follows documented wall-clock/timezone behavior.
- Aggregations use profile timezone unless a record requires another domain timezone.
- Tests must cover DST/timezone boundaries where relevant.
- Never assume every day has exactly 24 local hours.

---

title: 13. Secret handling rules
text:
## 13. Secret handling rules

Secrets include:

- AI API keys,
- OAuth access/refresh tokens,
- encryption keys,
- passwords/PIN derivatives,
- service credentials.

title: Never
text:
### Never

- commit secrets to Git,
- place them in `.env.example` as real values,
- store them in normal database fields without approved encryption design,
- store them in browser localStorage,
- send them to analytics,
- print them in console/server logs,
- include them in error messages,
- put them in query-string URLs,
- include them in AI prompts.

title: Required
text:
### Required

- platform secure storage/keychain where available,
- encrypted fallback where web constraints require it,
- redaction in diagnostics,
- secret-scanning test/check in CI when available.

---

title: 14. Authentication rules
text:
## 14. Authentication rules

Local profile authentication and cloud authentication are distinct concepts.

title: Local
text:
### Local

- email is not required,
- PIN/password/biometric may protect a profile,
- never store raw password/PIN,
- use approved password/KDF primitives,
- lock session according to product/platform behavior.

title: Cloud — future
text:
### Cloud — future

- identity is derived from authenticated server session/token,
- never trust client-supplied `user_id` as authorization,
- enforce authorization server-side,
- use row-level/user-level access controls where suitable.

---

title: 15. AI provider rules
text:
## 15. AI provider rules

AI integration must go through the provider-neutral AI layer.

title: Provider adapters own
text:
### Provider adapters own

- authentication format,
- provider request/response translation,
- streaming mechanics,
- provider error mapping,
- capability detection.

title: Product logic owns
text:
### Product logic owns

- permissions,
- context selection,
- proposal format,
- user approval,
- domain validation,
- persistence.

Never let provider-specific SDK objects leak into the domain model.

---

title: 16. AI context rules
text:
## 16. AI context rules

Before sending context to an external model:

- confirm active profile,
- gather only data relevant to the request,
- respect disabled history/memory/module settings,
- exclude credentials and secret metadata,
- treat health/journal content conservatively,
- disclose external processing in the UI,
- avoid sending an entire lifetime history when a narrow time window is enough.

Local model usage may permit broader private context, but still obeys profile and user permission rules.

---

title: 17. AI memory rules
text:
## 17. AI memory rules

AI memory and conversation history are separate stores/semantics.

Required capabilities when memory is implemented:

- local by default,
- profile-scoped,
- disable capture,
- inspect user-facing memory or summary,
- delete individual user-facing memory entries where product supports it,
- clear all memory,
- clear chats independently where schema allows.

A model-generated memory candidate should not become durable blindly. Use validation/retention rules and preserve provenance.

---

title: 18. Agent write rules
text: ## 18. Agent write rules

title: Read-only operations
text:
### Read-only operations

May run without a write approval prompt if the user asked for the analysis and the data is within granted scope.

title: Proposed writes
text:
### Proposed writes

AI/agents may generate a structured proposal.

title: Consequential writes
text:
### Consequential writes

Examples:

- creating many calendar events,
- rescheduling the week,
- changing a goal,
- deleting records,
- updating progress based on a reflection,
- writing to an external calendar.

These require preview/approval according to product policy.

title: Destructive operations
text:
### Destructive operations

Deletion, bulk destructive changes, irreversible external side effects, and credential/account changes require explicit confirmation.

title: Forbidden
text:
### Forbidden

- LLM executes raw SQL,
- LLM receives unrestricted repository object,
- LLM-generated prose is reparsed after approval as a new action plan,
- hidden writes during a chat response.

---

title: 19. AI proposal rules
text:
## 19. AI proposal rules

A proposal should be structured, validated, and reviewable.

It must include enough information to test and safely apply:

- affected records or intended new records,
- dates/times,
- reason,
- conflicts,
- operations (`create`, `update`, `delete`),
- dependencies,
- warnings,
- provenance.

Approval applies to a specific proposal version. If the proposal materially changes, approval must be obtained again.

---

title: 20. Reflection and wellbeing rules
text:
## 20. Reflection and wellbeing rules

Omnivae is not a punishment engine.

- Do not shame users for missed tasks.
- Do not automatically overload tomorrow because today was missed.
- Preserve user narrative separately from AI interpretation.
- Treat AI summaries as generated content, not the historical source of truth.
- Use actual evidence for progress.
- Present wellbeing patterns as observations with uncertainty.
- Do not present the app as diagnosing or treating medical conditions.
- Do not send health/reflection content to external AI without clear user-controlled scope.

---

title: 21. Health data rules
text:
## 21. Health data rules

Health data receives stricter handling.

- Import is opt-in.
- Request only required permissions/metric types.
- Preserve source attribution.
- Deduplicate imports using source identifiers and documented rules.
- Do not fabricate missing metrics.
- Do not convert incompatible units without tested conversion logic.
- Do not silently merge contradictory sources.
- Keep imported history locally accessible after successful import where allowed.
- Never claim a health insight is a medical diagnosis.
- Health-specific tests are mandatory before completing an integration.

---

title: 22. Calendar rules
text:
## 22. Calendar rules

Bulk schedule operations must be planned before committing.

For day/week/range copy:

1. Read source schedule.
2. Transform into destination plan.
3. Detect invalid date/time/conflict conditions.
4. Present or validate preview.
5. Commit atomically.
6. Emit provenance/bulk-operation metadata.
7. Test source remains unchanged.

Do not perform a loop of independent writes that leaves half a week pasted if one middle write fails, unless the operation explicitly supports partial success and the UI communicates it.

---

title: 23. Notes conversion rules
text:
## 23. Notes conversion rules

Converting a note to a task/event/goal:

- does not delete the source note,
- preserves a link/provenance reference,
- validates structured fields,
- lets the user review AI-extracted fields if AI is involved,
- does not silently schedule content based only on ambiguous prose.

---

title: 24. Progress and analytics rules
text:
## 24. Progress and analytics rules

- Raw completion/session/sample records are the source of truth.
- Percentages are derived or explicitly user-entered with provenance.
- AI cannot mark progress based on inference alone.
- Cached aggregates must be rebuildable.
- Changing dashboard filters never changes source data.
- Aggregation test cases must cover timezone boundaries and deleted/edited source records.

---

title: 25. Dependency rules
text:
## 25. Dependency rules

Before adding a dependency:

- verify active maintenance and compatibility,
- prefer mature, narrowly scoped libraries,
- avoid duplicate libraries for the same purpose,
- inspect license suitability,
- avoid dependencies requiring unnecessary network/cloud coupling,
- document major architectural dependencies.

Do not implement custom cryptography, recurrence parsing, or security-sensitive primitives when a trusted standard implementation exists.

---

title: 26. UI implementation rules
text:
## 26. UI implementation rules

- Core actions must expose loading/success/error states.
- Network-dependent UI must show offline/pending state.
- Destructive operations must be distinguishable.
- Disabled modules must not appear as broken navigable screens.
- Responsive behavior is tested at mobile and desktop/tablet widths for relevant features.
- Do not encode business rules only in presentation components.
- Preserve keyboard/accessibility semantics for core controls.

---

title: 27. Accessibility rules
text:
## 27. Accessibility rules

New core UI must support where applicable:

- semantic labels,
- keyboard navigation,
- focus visibility/order,
- adequate touch targets,
- non-color-only status cues,
- screen-reader-compatible controls.

Accessibility failures block completion when covered by the feature's acceptance criteria/test suite.

---

title: 28. Error handling rules
text:
## 28. Error handling rules

- Never swallow exceptions with an empty catch.
- Map technical errors to actionable user states.
- Keep raw provider errors out of user UI when they expose secrets/internal details.
- Preserve user-entered text when a save/network operation fails when possible.
- Log safely with redaction.
- Retry only when the operation is safe/idempotent.

---

title: 29. Logging and telemetry rules
text:
## 29. Logging and telemetry rules

Never log raw:

- API keys/tokens,
- passwords/PINs,
- encryption keys,
- journal text,
- AI chat content by default,
- raw health data by default.

Remote analytics/telemetry, if introduced, must have a privacy review and must not become required for product functionality.

---

title: 30. Migration rules
text:
## 30. Migration rules

For every schema migration:

- increment schema version,
- document old → new shape,
- write migration code,
- write fixture-based upgrade tests,
- test empty DB and populated DB,
- test failed migration behavior,
- preserve user data unless explicit deletion is part of the requirement,
- update `schema.md`.

A migration is not complete merely because a fresh install works.

---

title: 31. Sync rules — when implemented
text:
## 31. Sync rules — when implemented

- Local is not treated as a disposable cache.
- Every syncable entity has stable identity/version semantics.
- Deletions have tombstones or equivalent propagation semantics.
- Offline changes enter an outbox.
- Retries are idempotent.
- Conflicts follow an entity-specific documented policy.
- A user deletion must not be resurrected by an old remote copy.
- Authentication/authorization must not use a client-supplied owner ID.

---

title: 32. Test rules
text:
## 32. Test rules

Read `testing.md` for the complete matrix. At minimum:

- new behavior gets tests,
- bug fixes get a regression test,
- repository adapters pass conformance tests,
- profile-sensitive features get isolation tests,
- offline-capable features get offline tests,
- migrations get upgrade tests,
- AI agent writes get approval/validation tests,
- health imports get dedupe/source/unit tests,
- calendar bulk operations get atomicity/conflict/date tests.

Do not mock away the exact behavior the test is supposed to validate.

---

title: 33. Test-failure rules
text:
## 33. Test-failure rules

When a test fails:

1. Record the failure.
2. Determine whether implementation or test expectation is wrong.
3. Compare expectation to PRD/architecture.
4. Fix the wrong layer.
5. Re-run the failing test.
6. Re-run the required suite.
7. Keep status incomplete until all required tests pass.

Never:

- comment out the test,
- change expected output to the broken output without product justification,
- mark it flaky without evidence,
- skip it in CI to meet a deadline.

---

title: 34. `memory.md` update rules
text:
## 34. `memory.md` update rules

At the end of a meaningful implementation session, update `memory.md` with:

- date/time or session label,
- scope worked on,
- files/modules changed,
- migrations created,
- tests added/updated,
- exact test commands run,
- pass/fail summary,
- current task statuses,
- blockers/open questions,
- next recommended action.

Do not write vague entries such as “worked on dashboard.”

Do not mark something completed in memory without test evidence.

---

title: 35. Phase rules
text:
## 35. Phase rules

Follow `phases.md` unless an explicit product decision changes sequencing.

A later phase may be prototyped behind a feature flag, but it cannot silently become a dependency of an earlier phase.

A phase gate passes only when:

- its required features meet acceptance criteria,
- its required tests pass,
- migration/security/offline gates pass,
- `memory.md` reflects actual status.

---

title: 36. Documentation rules
text:
## 36. Documentation rules

Code changes must update docs when they change:

- product behavior,
- architecture,
- schema,
- test requirements,
- implementation phase status,
- locked/open decisions.

Do not let docs become fictional future state while code behaves differently. Use labels such as `planned`, `implemented_unverified`, and `completed`.

---

title: 37. Git/commit rules for agents
text:
## 37. Git/commit rules for agents

When the environment supports Git:

- inspect diff before completion,
- do not commit secrets/generated credentials,
- keep commits scoped where practical,
- include migrations and tests with the feature they support,
- do not rewrite unrelated history,
- do not force-push unless explicitly instructed.

Suggested commit style:

```text
feat(calendar): add atomic day schedule copy
fix(storage): enforce profile scope in note lookup
test(ai): cover approval rejection for planner proposals
docs(schema): add AI memory provenance fields
```

---

title: 38. Definition of ready
text:
## 38. Definition of ready

A task is ready for implementation when the agent can identify:

- desired behavior,
- acceptance criteria,
- affected module(s),
- data impact,
- security/profile impact,
- offline impact,
- required test categories.

If one is truly unspecified and blocks a safe implementation, record it in `memory.md` as an open decision. For non-critical implementation details, choose the lowest-risk solution consistent with the existing architecture and document it.

---

title: 39. Definition of done
text:
## 39. Definition of done

A task is **done only when all are true**:

- [ ] Acceptance criteria satisfied.
- [ ] Code follows architecture boundaries.
- [ ] Profile isolation preserved.
- [ ] Offline behavior handled where applicable.
- [ ] Security/privacy rules satisfied.
- [ ] Schema/migrations updated if needed.
- [ ] Unit tests pass.
- [ ] Integration tests required by scope pass.
- [ ] E2E tests required by scope pass.
- [ ] Regression tests pass.
- [ ] Static/type/lint checks pass according to project CI.
- [ ] No required test is skipped/quarantined.
- [ ] Documentation is updated.
- [ ] `memory.md` contains test evidence and accurate status.

If any checkbox is false, status is not `completed`.

---

title: 40. Agent handoff rule
text:
## 40. Agent handoff rule

When stopping work, leave the next agent enough context to continue without re-deriving state.

The handoff must state:

- what was requested,
- what is implemented,
- what is only partially implemented,
- what tests pass/fail,
- exact failing test names/errors if relevant,
- data migration state,
- open decisions,
- next safe step.

Never claim a cleaner state than reality.

---

title: 41. Final rule
text:
## 41. Final rule

When uncertain whether to optimize for speed or preserve a core Omnivae invariant, preserve the invariant and document the trade-off.

When uncertain whether a feature is complete, it is **not complete until the required tests prove it**.

title: Omnivae — Product Requirements Document (PRD)
text:
# Omnivae — Product Requirements Document (PRD)

> Status: Active product source of truth  
> Product name: **Omnivae**  
> Document version: 1.0  
> Last consolidated: 2026-09-08  
> Audience: Product owner, AGY/coding agents, designers, engineers, QA

title: 0. How an implementation agent must use this document
text:
## 0. How an implementation agent must use this document

This PRD defines **what Omnivae must do and why**. It does not grant permission to improvise architecture, security, or completion criteria.

Implementation agents must also read, in this order:

1. `rules.md` — non-negotiable implementation rules.
2. `prd.md` — product behavior and acceptance criteria.
3. `architecture.md` — system boundaries, flows, and technical architecture.
4. `schema.md` — data model and persistence contracts.
5. `phases.md` — implementation sequence and gates.
6. `testing.md` — required test matrix and definition of done.
7. `memory.md` — current implementation state, decisions, blockers, and next work.

If documents conflict, follow the precedence rules in `rules.md`. Do not silently choose a different interpretation.

---

title: 1. Product summary
text:
## 1. Product summary

**Omnivae is a local-first personal intelligence and life-orchestration system.** It helps a person plan, think, track health and progress, reflect on what actually happened, and adapt future plans without taking control away from the user.

It is **not** merely:

- a task manager,
- a calendar,
- a habit tracker,
- a health dashboard,
- a journaling app,
- or an AI chatbot.

Its core differentiation is the connection between those systems. Omnivae should understand the user's goals, current plans, actual behavior, reflections, and wellbeing signals, then help the user make better next decisions.

title: Product principle
text:
### Product principle

> Omnivae helps a person become who they are trying to become while keeping control of their data, choices, and attention.

title: Five product pillars
text:
### Five product pillars

1. **Plan** — calendar, tasks, goals, routines, notes, projects.
2. **Think** — AI chat, memory, research support, decision support.
3. **Health** — sleep, activity, workouts, nutrition/water and wearable-derived signals when available.
4. **Reflect** — journal, daily story, nightly AI reflection, context-aware progress review.
5. **Grow** — study, skills, habits, projects, long-term progress and adaptive planning.

---

title: 2. Product goals
text: ## 2. Product goals

title: G1 — Local-first independence
text:
### G1 — Local-first independence

The core product must remain useful without a cloud account and without a network connection.

A local-only user must be able to create a profile, unlock it locally, use core modules, store data, and revisit their history without creating a server account.

title: G2 — One connected personal system
text:
### G2 — One connected personal system

A user should be able to move information between modules rather than re-enter it. Examples:

- convert a note into a task,
- convert a note into a calendar event,
- connect a task to a goal,
- connect a study session to a skill or goal,
- connect a workout to health progress,
- reference a reflection when adapting a future plan.

title: G3 — Adaptive rather than punitive planning
text:
### G3 — Adaptive rather than punitive planning

Omnivae must distinguish between planned behavior and actual life. Missed work should not automatically be framed as failure.

When circumstances change, the system should help the user understand what happened and adapt future plans.

title: G4 — Health and wellbeing as a first-class pillar
text:
### G4 — Health and wellbeing as a first-class pillar

Health is not an optional decorative chart. Omnivae should provide meaningful health visibility and, where possible, integrate with device/platform health sources.

The system may surface potential wellbeing concerns or patterns, but should do so supportively and with clear uncertainty rather than acting as a medical authority.

title: G5 — User-owned AI
text:
### G5 — User-owned AI

AI must be provider-agnostic. Users may bring their own cloud API keys or configure local models. Chat history and AI memory are local by default.

title: G6 — Cross-platform product logic
text:
### G6 — Cross-platform product logic

The product should share domain logic across web/PWA and mobile wrappers, with responsive experiences for phone, tablet, and desktop-sized screens.

title: G7 — Modular product
text:
### G7 — Modular product

Not everyone needs every life domain. Users must be able to enable/disable optional modules and dashboard widgets. **Job/Career must never be mandatory.**

---

title: 3. Non-goals for the initial product
text:
## 3. Non-goals for the initial product

The initial product must not be derailed by premature infrastructure or breadth.

Do not make these initial requirements:

- Kubernetes,
- Kafka,
- microservices,
- database sharding,
- multi-region infrastructure,
- a custom cryptographic algorithm,
- autonomous agents with unrestricted write access,
- mandatory managed cloud accounts,
- mandatory wearable ownership,
- a full financial platform,
- collaboration/social network features,
- a medical diagnosis product,
- a universal plugin marketplace before core workflows are stable.

These may be revisited through explicit architectural decisions later.

---

title: 4. Target users
text: ## 4. Target users

title: 4.1 Primary user — self-directed individual
text:
### 4.1 Primary user — self-directed individual

A person who wants one system to organize life domains while retaining privacy and control.

Typical needs:

- plan days and weeks,
- work toward long-term goals,
- study or build skills,
- exercise and track wellbeing,
- collect notes and thoughts,
- review progress,
- use AI for planning and reflection,
- avoid scattering personal context across many apps.

title: 4.2 Privacy-sensitive user
text:
### 4.2 Privacy-sensitive user

A user who wants most personal records stored locally and wants explicit control over what leaves the device.

title: 4.3 Multi-profile household/device user
text:
### 4.3 Multi-profile household/device user

A device may contain multiple isolated local profiles. Each profile must have independent settings, data, AI credentials, and history.

title: 4.4 Optional domain users
text:
### 4.4 Optional domain users

Some users may use Study but not Career. Some may use Gym but not Diet. Some may use only core planning and notes. The product must not assume employment, gym attendance, wearable ownership, or a specific life path.

---

title: 5. Product experience principles
text: ## 5. Product experience principles

title: P1 — Calm, premium, information-dense when useful
text:
### P1 — Calm, premium, information-dense when useful

The UI should feel polished and intentional. It should avoid the visual feeling of a spreadsheet-like tracker unless the user deliberately enters an analytics-heavy view.

title: P2 — User controls automation
text:
### P2 — User controls automation

AI may recommend or prepare changes. It must not silently perform consequential writes that materially alter a user's schedule, goals, data, or external services.

title: P3 — Context matters
text:
### P3 — Context matters

A missed gym session because of a family situation should be treated differently from a repeated pattern the user wants to change. Reflection and progress logic should preserve context.

title: P4 — One underlying truth
text:
### P4 — One underlying truth

Daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly views must aggregate from the same underlying records. Do not maintain separate inconsistent progress systems.

title: P5 — Offline is a normal state
text:
### P5 — Offline is a normal state

Offline mode is not an error mode. Network-dependent features should degrade explicitly and preserve local work.

title: P6 — Privacy is visible
text:
### P6 — Privacy is visible

The UI must make it understandable when data remains local and when a prompt, sync payload, or external integration leaves the device.

---

title: 6. Core information architecture
text: ## 6. Core information architecture

title: Core modules
text:
### Core modules

- Dashboard
- Calendar
- Tasks
- Goals
- Notes
- AI Chat
- Analytics / Progress
- Settings
- Files

title: First-class or high-priority optional modules
text:
### First-class or high-priority optional modules

- Journal / Reflection
- Health
- Study
- Gym / Workouts
- Habits / Routines
- Projects

title: Future/optional modules
text:
### Future/optional modules

- Diet / Nutrition
- Career / Job
- Reading
- Finance
- Travel
- Languages
- Relationships
- Custom modules / plugins

A disabled optional module must not block other modules.

---

title: 7. Account, profile, and launch requirements
text: ## 7. Account, profile, and launch requirements

title: 7.1 Launch flow
text:
### 7.1 Launch flow

At launch, the app should support:

- existing local profile selection,
- local profile creation,
- guest/local temporary access where supported,
- optional cloud account sign-in when cloud functionality exists.

title: 7.2 Local profile
text:
### 7.2 Local profile

A local profile must be usable without email.

Supported local protection modes may include:

- password,
- PIN,
- biometrics where the platform supports them.

title: 7.3 Multi-profile isolation
text:
### 7.3 Multi-profile isolation

Each profile has separate:

- module configuration,
- dashboard layout,
- tasks,
- calendar,
- goals,
- notes,
- journal/reflections,
- health/workout/study data,
- AI conversations,
- AI memory,
- AI provider configuration,
- encrypted credentials,
- sync settings.

A profile must never be able to read another profile's protected records through UI, application APIs, storage adapters, export, search, or AI context retrieval.

title: 7.4 Guest behavior
text:
### 7.4 Guest behavior

Guest behavior must be explicit. If guest data is temporary, the UI must say so before data loss can occur. If guest data persists locally, it must be treated as its own isolated profile.

---

title: 8. Dashboard requirements
text: ## 8. Dashboard requirements

title: 8.1 Purpose
text:
### 8.1 Purpose

The dashboard is the user's high-level command center, not a fixed home screen.

title: 8.2 Required behavior
text:
### 8.2 Required behavior

Users can:

- enable/disable widgets,
- rearrange supported widgets,
- choose relevant modules,
- switch or filter progress by day/week/month/year where applicable,
- see current priorities and today's schedule,
- see progress summaries derived from underlying records,
- access AI assistance without losing the context of the dashboard.

title: 8.3 Candidate widgets
text:
### 8.3 Candidate widgets

- Today's tasks
- Calendar / next events
- Goals
- Habits / routines
- Study
- Gym / workout
- Health summary
- Reflection / journal prompt
- AI coach / assistant entry point
- Projects
- Career only if enabled

title: 8.4 Profile identity
text:
### 8.4 Profile identity

The user may set a profile picture/avatar and profile-level display preferences.

title: Acceptance criteria
text:
### Acceptance criteria

- Widget state survives app restart.
- Widget state is profile-scoped.
- Disabled modules do not leak into the dashboard.
- Progress values match source records.
- Time range changes do not create duplicate progress records.
- Dashboard works from local data when offline.

---

title: 9. Calendar and scheduling requirements
text: ## 9. Calendar and scheduling requirements

title: 9.1 Calendar fundamentals
text:
### 9.1 Calendar fundamentals

The calendar must support local events and be designed so external calendars can later be integrated through adapters.

Events may be associated with:

- tasks,
- goals,
- projects,
- notes,
- study sessions,
- workouts,
- routines/templates.

title: 9.2 Schedule copy/paste
text:
### 9.2 Schedule copy/paste

This is a core productivity behavior and must not be reduced to duplicating one event at a time.

The user must eventually be able to:

- copy an entire day's schedule,
- paste the copied schedule to another day,
- paste the same day schedule to multiple selected days,
- create different weekday and weekend patterns,
- copy an entire week,
- paste a week to another week,
- repeat copied schedules forward across a range,
- support longer scheduling windows such as multiple months,
- preview conflicts before committing a bulk copy,
- undo or cancel a bulk operation when feasible.

Example behavior:

- Copy Monday's schedule.
- Paste to Tuesday and Friday.
- Keep a separate Saturday/Sunday pattern.
- Copy a whole completed week and apply it to selected future weeks.

title: 9.3 Schedule templates
text:
### 9.3 Schedule templates

Templates should support reusable patterns such as:

- office routine,
- study routine,
- weekend routine,
- workout week,
- exam preparation,
- project sprint.

Templates must remain editable after application. Applying a template creates or links records according to the defined implementation contract; it must not make ordinary calendar data impossible to edit.

title: 9.4 AI scheduling
text:
### 9.4 AI scheduling

The AI planner should be able to produce a **proposed** schedule based on:

- goals,
- tasks,
- deadlines,
- calendar availability,
- existing routines,
- user constraints,
- recent progress/reflection context when permission is granted.

The flow is:

`User intent → gather allowed context → generate proposal → show diff/preview → user approves → write schedule`

The AI must avoid obvious conflicts and should explain material trade-offs.

title: 9.5 Adaptive rescheduling
text:
### 9.5 Adaptive rescheduling

When the user misses or changes planned work, Omnivae may offer to rebalance remaining work. The user should not be forced into a cascading punitive schedule.

title: Acceptance criteria
text:
### Acceptance criteria

- Bulk copy does not mutate the source schedule.
- Repeated paste honors timezone/date boundaries.
- Conflicts are detectable before commit.
- Cancellation or failure leaves the database consistent.
- AI writes are blocked until required approval occurs.
- Offline local scheduling remains available.

---

title: 10. Tasks requirements
text:
## 10. Tasks requirements

Tasks should support at minimum:

- title,
- description/details,
- status,
- priority,
- due date/time,
- optional scheduled start/end,
- optional goal/project relationship,
- optional note source,
- tags/labels if implemented,
- recurrence when recurrence engine is ready,
- completion history.

Task status should distinguish at least:

- pending/open,
- in progress where supported,
- completed,
- cancelled/skipped.

A missed due date must not equal completed or permanently failed.

title: Acceptance criteria
text:
### Acceptance criteria

- Completion is stored as a durable event/state transition.
- A task linked from another module maintains referential integrity.
- Deleting a linked source does not silently destroy unrelated records.
- Profile isolation is enforced.
- Offline task creation/edit/completion works.

---

title: 11. Goals and progress requirements
text:
## 11. Goals and progress requirements

Goals are longer-horizon outcomes that can connect to tasks, habits, projects, study, health, or other evidence.

A goal may include:

- title,
- description,
- target date,
- status,
- progress strategy,
- parent/child hierarchy,
- milestones,
- linked evidence,
- reflection/context.

title: Progress model
text:
### Progress model

Do not rely only on a manually entered percentage. Progress may be derived from evidence depending on goal type.

Examples:

- completed milestones,
- study time,
- project tasks,
- workout consistency,
- habit completions,
- user-confirmed qualitative progress.

AI may summarize progress but must not fabricate completion evidence.

---

title: 12. Notes requirements
text:
## 12. Notes requirements

Notes are a capture surface and a source of structured actions.

title: 12.1 Required baseline
text:
### 12.1 Required baseline

- create/edit/delete notes,
- local search,
- timestamps,
- profile scope,
- optional pin/favorite/tag metadata,
- link to relevant entities.

title: 12.2 Conversion flows
text:
### 12.2 Conversion flows

A user should be able to convert or extract a note into one or more of:

- task,
- calendar event,
- goal,
- project item,
- journal/reflection entry.

The original note should remain available unless the user deletes it.

title: 12.3 Rich content direction
text:
### 12.3 Rich content direction

The architecture should not prevent future support for:

- markdown/rich text,
- images,
- attached files/PDFs,
- voice capture/transcription,
- drawing/stylus input.

These are staged features, not all MVP requirements.

---

title: 13. Files requirements
text:
## 13. Files requirements

The Files module is a user-visible inventory for local attachments and future synced assets.

It should support a metadata layer that can associate a file with notes, journal entries, projects, AI conversations, or other entities without duplicating the binary unnecessarily.

Requirements:

- profile-scoped metadata,
- clear local vs synced state,
- MIME/type and size metadata,
- safe deletion semantics,
- no exposing another profile's attachments,
- future content indexing through opt-in processing.

---

title: 14. Journal and nightly reflection requirements
text: ## 14. Journal and nightly reflection requirements

title: 14.1 Journal
text:
### 14.1 Journal

Users must be able to create text-based journal/reflection entries. Voice can be added when the platform capability is implemented.

title: 14.2 Nightly reflection concept
text:
### 14.2 Nightly reflection concept

Omnivae should support a nightly reflection flow that helps the user tell the story of the day rather than merely checking boxes.

The user may say, for example:

- what they completed,
- what they skipped,
- what unexpected events occurred,
- how they felt,
- what mattered,
- what should change tomorrow.

title: 14.3 AI behavior
text:
### 14.3 AI behavior

The reflection assistant may:

- summarize the day,
- ask relevant follow-up questions,
- identify likely updates to tasks/progress,
- propose journal highlights,
- propose schedule adaptations,
- identify repeated patterns,
- preserve meaningful context.

It must distinguish **proposals** from **confirmed updates**. User-authored narrative must not be overwritten by an AI summary.

title: 14.4 Tone and wellbeing
text:
### 14.4 Tone and wellbeing

Reflection must not shame the user. The system should prioritize sustainable improvement and wellbeing over perfect schedule adherence.

title: Acceptance criteria
text:
### Acceptance criteria

- Reflection can be saved locally.
- AI is optional; manual journaling still works.
- AI-derived updates indicate their source.
- Consequential changes require confirmation according to `rules.md`.
- User can edit/delete the reflection and AI summary according to retention rules.

---

title: 15. AI chat requirements
text: ## 15. AI chat requirements

title: 15.1 Provider-agnostic AI
text:
### 15.1 Provider-agnostic AI

The AI layer must support adapters so providers can be added without hard-coding product logic to one vendor.

Target provider classes include:

- hosted API providers,
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints,
- local model runtimes such as Ollama/LM Studio class integrations.

Concrete provider support is phase-dependent.

title: 15.2 BYOK
text:
### 15.2 BYOK

Users may enter their own provider credentials.

Credentials must:

- be validated when feasible,
- be stored with platform secure storage or encrypted fallback,
- never be logged,
- never be committed to source,
- never appear in analytics,
- never be placed in URLs.

title: 15.3 Local-by-default conversation storage
text:
### 15.3 Local-by-default conversation storage

Users can:

- delete one conversation,
- delete all conversations,
- export chats,
- disable chat history,
- control whether chat data is eligible for sync.

title: 15.4 AI memory
text:
### 15.4 AI memory

AI memory is separate from raw chat history.

Users must be able to:

- see memory entries or a meaningful memory summary,
- delete individual user-facing memories where supported by the product model,
- clear all Omnivae AI memory,
- disable memory capture,
- keep chats while clearing memory or clear chats while keeping explicitly retained memory, if the schema supports this separation.

AI memory must be profile-scoped and local by default.

title: 15.5 External data disclosure
text:
### 15.5 External data disclosure

Before or during use of an external AI provider, the UI must make clear that the submitted prompt/context is processed by that provider.

---

title: 16. AI agent requirements
text: ## 16. AI agent requirements

title: 16.1 Controlled tools
text:
### 16.1 Controlled tools

Agents must operate through explicit tool contracts, not arbitrary database access.

Tool categories may include:

- read goals,
- read tasks,
- read calendar,
- read selected notes/reflections,
- propose schedule,
- create/update tasks after approval,
- create/update events after approval,
- summarize progress.

title: 16.2 Approval model
text:
### 16.2 Approval model

Default rule:

- read-only analysis may proceed if the user granted access to that data,
- proposed writes must be previewed,
- significant writes require user approval,
- destructive actions require explicit confirmation,
- external side effects require explicit permission and integration-specific safeguards.

title: 16.3 Progress intelligence
text:
### 16.3 Progress intelligence

The long-term AI differentiator is not generic conversation. It is a loop such as:

`Goal → current state → gap → plan → schedule → action/evidence → reflection → progress review → next plan`

The AI must rely on actual stored evidence and user-confirmed context rather than inventing accomplishments.

---

title: 17. Health requirements
text: ## 17. Health requirements

title: 17.1 Product importance
text:
### 17.1 Product importance

Health is a first-class pillar of Omnivae and should receive product quality comparable to planning and AI.

title: 17.2 Health dashboard direction
text:
### 17.2 Health dashboard direction

The system should be designed to represent data such as:

- steps/activity,
- heart rate,
- sleep,
- workouts,
- calories/energy where available,
- water,
- weight/BMI where user-entered or supplied,
- SpO2 where available,
- stress/readiness-style signals where a source provides them,
- temperature where a source provides it,
- nutrition summaries.

Not every source supplies every metric. Missing metrics must not be fabricated.

title: 17.3 Data sources and integrations
text:
### 17.3 Data sources and integrations

Future integration targets may include platform and vendor health ecosystems, for example:

- Android Health Connect,
- Apple Health,
- Fitbit,
- Garmin,
- Samsung Health,
- Xiaomi/Mi Fitness ecosystems,
- Amazfit/Zepp,
- Polar,
- direct BLE devices where technically and legally appropriate.

The system should prefer platform health aggregation APIs where appropriate rather than building a bespoke integration for every device in the first release.

title: 17.4 Consent and privacy
text:
### 17.4 Consent and privacy

Health import must be opt-in and permission-scoped. Omnivae must not silently send health data to a cloud AI model.

title: 17.5 Wellbeing insights
text:
### 17.5 Wellbeing insights

Omnivae may detect patterns such as:

- repeated short sleep,
- sustained overwork,
- skipped meals if tracked,
- declining activity,
- repeated missed workouts.

The product should frame these as observations and choices, not diagnoses.

---

title: 18. Study and skill growth requirements
text:
## 18. Study and skill growth requirements

The Study module may include:

- topics,
- study sessions,
- planned vs actual study time,
- resources,
- linked goals/projects,
- skill tracking.

A future skill graph can model:

`Goal → required skills → resources → projects/evidence → skill progress`

Study progress must be grounded in recorded sessions/evidence or explicit user confirmation.

---

title: 19. Gym/workout requirements
text:
## 19. Gym/workout requirements

The Gym module should support structured workout tracking without requiring a wearable.

Baseline model:

- workout session,
- exercise,
- sets,
- repetitions,
- load/weight,
- duration when applicable,
- notes,
- timestamps.

Future health imports may complement manual workout records but must avoid uncontrolled duplicate creation.

---

title: 20. Habits and routines requirements
text:
## 20. Habits and routines requirements

Habits/routines are recurring behaviors distinct from one-off tasks.

The system should support:

- recurrence definition,
- completion records,
- streak/statistics derived from completions,
- pausing/archiving,
- optional relationship to goals.

Do not store a streak as the only source of truth; derive it from completion records.

---

title: 21. Analytics and progress requirements
text:
## 21. Analytics and progress requirements

The system should aggregate from source records into:

- daily,
- weekly,
- monthly,
- yearly views.

Examples:

- study duration,
- task completion,
- habit adherence,
- workout frequency/volume,
- goal evidence,
- health trends.

Rules:

- aggregation must be reproducible,
- raw/source records remain the source of truth,
- computed summaries may be cached but must be rebuildable,
- timezone boundaries must be respected,
- a UI filter must not mutate history.

---

title: 22. Search requirements
text:
## 22. Search requirements

The product should evolve toward cross-module search while preserving profile boundaries.

Search may cover:

- notes,
- tasks,
- goals,
- calendar events,
- journal entries,
- projects,
- AI conversation titles/messages according to history settings,
- files metadata.

AI semantic retrieval is a later layer. Core exact/text search must not require a remote model.

---

title: 23. Notifications and reminders
text:
## 23. Notifications and reminders

Notifications are phase-dependent, but the domain model must allow:

- task reminders,
- calendar reminders,
- habit/routine reminders,
- nightly reflection prompt,
- schedule change notifications,
- future sync/integration status alerts.

Local notifications should be preferred where a cloud service is not necessary.

---

title: 24. Offline requirements
text:
## 24. Offline requirements

When offline, a local profile should still be able to:

- unlock the app,
- view dashboards,
- create/edit/complete tasks,
- create/edit calendar events,
- track habits,
- create/edit notes,
- create journal entries,
- log workouts/study,
- view locally stored health history,
- review local AI chats,
- use a local model if configured,
- queue future sync changes when sync exists.

Network-only actions must show a clear unavailable/pending state rather than failing silently.

---

title: 25. Sync and cloud requirements
text: ## 25. Sync and cloud requirements

title: 25.1 Local-first default
text:
### 25.1 Local-first default

Managed cloud sync is not required for the earliest product phase.

title: 25.2 Future sync modes
text:
### 25.2 Future sync modes

The architecture should permit:

1. local only,
2. user-owned cloud/backup,
3. optional managed Omnivae cloud.

title: 25.3 Sync correctness
text:
### 25.3 Sync correctness

When sync is implemented it must include:

- stable identifiers,
- versioning,
- outbox/change log,
- retry behavior,
- deletion tombstones,
- conflict detection,
- explicit conflict strategy,
- profile/account authorization,
- encrypted transport.

Sync must not make the local database a disposable cache. Local remains a first-class data store.

---

title: 26. Settings requirements
text:
## 26. Settings requirements

Settings should include clear categories such as:

- profile and local security,
- modules,
- dashboard layout,
- appearance/preferences,
- AI providers/models,
- AI memory/history,
- data export/deletion,
- privacy and permissions,
- health/device integrations,
- calendar integrations,
- sync/account,
- notifications,
- storage,
- about/system status,
- developer/debug options only when appropriate.

title: System status direction
text:
### System status direction

A system status view may show:

- local database state,
- selected AI provider/model,
- calendar integration state,
- health integration state,
- cloud sync state,
- notification permission/state,
- storage usage,
- Bluetooth/integration availability when relevant.

---

title: 27. Data portability and deletion
text:
## 27. Data portability and deletion

The user must have meaningful control over their records.

Design for:

- export of user data,
- deletion of one record,
- deletion of module data where appropriate,
- chat deletion,
- AI memory deletion,
- profile deletion,
- eventual cloud account deletion if managed cloud exists.

Deletion behavior must be explicit when sync/backup exists. Tombstones or remote propagation must not resurrect deliberately deleted data.

---

title: 28. Security and privacy requirements
text:
## 28. Security and privacy requirements

Minimum requirements:

- profile isolation,
- encrypted sensitive local data,
- secure credential storage,
- no plaintext API keys in logs/source/analytics/URLs,
- no trusting client-supplied cloud user IDs,
- server-side authorization for cloud mode,
- TLS for network transport,
- explicit user permission for external integrations,
- least-privilege access where possible,
- safe export/deletion behavior,
- no hidden external transmission of personal context.

See `rules.md` and `architecture.md` for binding implementation constraints.

---

title: 29. Accessibility and responsive UX
text:
## 29. Accessibility and responsive UX

The UI should support:

- keyboard navigation on web/desktop-sized layouts,
- readable contrast and scalable text,
- touch targets suitable for mobile/tablet,
- responsive navigation,
- screen-reader semantics for core controls,
- stylus-friendly future note/drawing interaction on supported tablets.

Accessibility regressions count as product defects.

---

title: 30. Performance expectations
text:
## 30. Performance expectations

Exact budgets should be benchmarked by phase, but the product should follow these qualitative requirements:

- local CRUD feels immediate,
- dashboard does not trigger unnecessary AI/network calls,
- large histories use pagination/virtualization where needed,
- indexes support common profile/time/status queries,
- analytics use incremental/rebuildable aggregation rather than scanning the entire database on every render,
- offline startup remains functional after the app shell is installed/cached.

---

title: 31. Primary user journeys
text: ## 31. Primary user journeys

title: Journey A — First local use
text:
### Journey A — First local use

1. Open Omnivae.
2. Create local profile.
3. Choose PIN/password; optionally configure biometrics where available.
4. Select modules or accept defaults.
5. Land on dashboard.
6. Create first task/note/event without creating a cloud account.

title: Journey B — Plan a week
text:
### Journey B — Plan a week

1. Open Calendar.
2. Review existing commitments.
3. Create or apply routines/templates.
4. Copy a day or week pattern if needed.
5. Resolve conflicts.
6. Save.
7. Dashboard reflects planned work.

title: Journey C — AI plan proposal
text:
### Journey C — AI plan proposal

1. Tell AI a goal/deadline.
2. AI reads only allowed context.
3. AI prepares schedule/task proposal.
4. User reviews changes.
5. User approves selected changes.
6. Approved records are written atomically.
7. Audit/provenance indicates AI-assisted origin where appropriate.

title: Journey D — Nightly reflection
text:
### Journey D — Nightly reflection

1. User opens or receives a local reminder for reflection.
2. User tells the story of the day in text/voice when available.
3. AI summarizes and asks relevant follow-up questions.
4. AI proposes progress/task/calendar updates.
5. User confirms changes.
6. Reflection and confirmed updates are saved.
7. Future planning may use confirmed context.

title: Journey E — Health review
text:
### Journey E — Health review

1. User opens Health.
2. View local/manual/imported metrics.
3. See trends and source attribution.
4. Optionally ask AI about selected health context.
5. App clearly indicates what data will be shared with the selected provider.

title: Journey F — Note to action
text:
### Journey F — Note to action

1. User writes note.
2. Selects text or note action.
3. Converts to task/event/goal.
4. Reviews structured fields.
5. Saves.
6. New entity links back to source note.

---

title: 32. Functional priority map
text:
## 32. Functional priority map

Priority definitions:

- **P0** — required for a usable local-first foundation.
- **P1** — required for the first strong product release.
- **P2** — differentiating intelligence/integration layer.
- **P3** — future scale/ecosystem.

title: P0
text:
### P0

- product shell/navigation
- local profile
- local unlock
- storage abstraction
- profile isolation
- tasks
- calendar basic CRUD
- notes basic CRUD
- goals basic CRUD
- dashboard baseline
- settings baseline
- offline persistence
- import/export foundation
- test infrastructure

title: P1
text:
### P1

- multi-profile
- encryption/secure secrets
- modular dashboard
- habits/routines
- study
- gym
- journal/reflection manual mode
- files metadata/attachments
- daily/weekly/monthly/yearly analytics
- schedule copy/paste day/week
- schedule templates
- BYOK AI chat
- AI history controls
- AI memory controls baseline
- PWA/mobile packaging

title: P2
text:
### P2

- AI planning proposal engine
- nightly AI reflection
- adaptive rescheduling
- progress intelligence
- richer goal/skill graph
- health platform integrations
- external calendar adapters
- local model integrations
- user-owned sync/backup
- voice workflows
- richer notes/stylus

title: P3
text:
### P3

- managed Omnivae cloud
- automatic cross-device sync
- collaboration where appropriate
- plugin ecosystem
- broader vendor integrations
- paid cloud tier if product strategy chooses it

---

title: 33. Release-level acceptance gates
text:
## 33. Release-level acceptance gates

A release cannot be declared complete because screens exist.

It must satisfy all of the following:

1. Required feature behavior matches this PRD.
2. Architecture rules are not violated.
3. Schema migrations are valid.
4. Required tests in `testing.md` pass.
5. No P0 security/privacy defects remain open.
6. Offline behavior for the phase is verified.
7. Multi-profile isolation is verified for any multi-profile release.
8. No secrets are leaked into logs/build artifacts.
9. Accessibility smoke tests pass for new core flows.
10. `memory.md` is updated with what is actually complete, what failed, and what is next.

**Never mark a task, subtask, phase, feature, or release as completed unless its required test cases pass.**

---

title: 34. Open product decisions
text:
## 34. Open product decisions

These are intentionally not invented. An agent must not silently lock them without an explicit decision or ADR.

- Exact visual design system and component library.
- Exact database implementation details per platform beyond the storage abstraction baseline.
- Exact encryption library/key hierarchy.
- First external AI providers to ship.
- First health integration to ship.
- First calendar integration to ship.
- Whether guest profiles persist by default.
- Exact sync provider for user-owned backup.
- Managed cloud vendor stack, if/when P3 begins.
- Exact voice transcription and TTS providers.
- Monetization/pricing.

When one is decided, update `memory.md`, relevant specification files, and an ADR if architectural.

---

title: 35. Product terminology
text:
## 35. Product terminology

Use these terms consistently:

- **Profile** — local isolated user identity/data boundary on a device.
- **Cloud account** — optional remote authentication identity; not the same as a local profile.
- **Module** — functional life domain such as Study or Gym.
- **Widget** — dashboard component.
- **Source record** — original stored evidence such as a task completion or study session.
- **Aggregation** — derived daily/weekly/monthly/yearly summary.
- **AI conversation** — ordered AI/user messages.
- **AI memory** — durable structured context distinct from raw chat history.
- **Proposal** — AI-generated suggested changes not yet committed.
- **Approval** — explicit user authorization to commit a proposal.
- **Local-first** — local data and workflows remain first-class even when optional cloud exists.

---

title: 36. Final product statement for agents
text:
## 36. Final product statement for agents

When choosing between a shortcut and the product philosophy, preserve these invariants:

- local-first,
- privacy-first,
- profile isolation,
- modularity,
- user control over AI,
- health/wellbeing treated seriously,
- actual evidence over fabricated progress,
- adaptive planning over punishment,
- one connected data model,
- tests before completion.

If an implementation decision undermines one of these, stop and document the conflict instead of silently shipping it.

title: Omnivae — App Flow and Architecture
text:
# Omnivae — App Flow and Architecture

> Status: Architecture baseline  
> Version: 1.0  
> Last consolidated: 2026-09-08  
> Audience: AGY/coding agents, software engineers, reviewers

title: 0. Architecture mandate
text:
## 0. Architecture mandate

Omnivae is built as a **local-first, privacy-first, modular monolith with explicit ports/adapters**. It must work without a cloud account. Cloud sync, managed backend services, and broader integrations are additive layers, not assumptions baked into the domain.

The current baseline supersedes earlier exploratory stack ideas:

- **Web/PWA:** Next.js + React.
- **Mobile:** Capacitor wrappers around the shared web application where feasible.
- **Web local persistence:** IndexedDB through a storage adapter.
- **Mobile local persistence:** SQLite/local secure storage through a storage adapter.
- **Shared logic:** application/domain packages independent of platform persistence.
- **Cloud:** optional and deferred until a phase requires it.

Do not replace this stack casually. Architectural changes require an ADR and corresponding updates to this document, `schema.md`, `phases.md`, and `memory.md`.

---

title: 1. Architectural principles
text:
## 1. Architectural principles

1. **Local-first:** local storage is authoritative for local-only operation.
2. **Offline-first UX:** offline is a supported mode, not an exceptional failure state.
3. **Profile isolation:** all personal data is scoped to a profile boundary.
4. **Ports and adapters:** domain logic does not import IndexedDB, SQLite, vendor SDKs, or cloud APIs directly.
5. **Modular monolith first:** prefer simple, well-defined internal modules over distributed services.
6. **Provider-agnostic AI:** AI capabilities depend on an internal interface, not one vendor.
7. **Controlled agents:** AI writes flow through validated domain commands and approval gates.
8. **Source records over derived state:** analytics/progress are derived from facts that can be recomputed.
9. **Stable IDs:** use UUID/ULID-class identifiers suitable for future sync.
10. **UTC internally + timezone context:** preserve correct local-day semantics while storing transport-safe timestamps.
11. **Secure secrets:** provider keys are never normal application data.
12. **Scale by evidence:** do not add microservices/Kafka/Kubernetes/sharding until actual constraints require them.

---

title: 2. System context
text:
## 2. System context

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U[User] --> APP[Omnivae App]
    APP --> LOCAL[(Local Profile Store)]
    APP --> SEC[Secure Credential Store]
    APP --> AIL[Local AI Runtime - optional]
    APP --> AIC[External AI Provider - optional]
    APP --> H[Health Platform / Wearable Adapter - optional]
    APP --> C[External Calendar Adapter - optional]
    APP --> SYNC[Sync Engine - future]
    SYNC --> UC[User-owned Cloud - future]
    SYNC --> OC[Omnivae Cloud - future]
```

The app must retain useful functionality when every external box is unavailable.

---

title: 3. High-level component architecture
text:
## 3. High-level component architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    UI[Presentation Layer\nNext.js/React UI] --> APP[Application Layer\nUse cases / commands / queries]
    APP --> DOM[Domain Layer\nEntities / policies / services]

    APP --> STORAGEPORT[Storage Ports]
    APP --> AIPORT[AI Ports]
    APP --> INTPORT[Integration Ports]
    APP --> NOTIFPORT[Notification Port]

    STORAGEPORT --> IDB[IndexedDB Adapter]
    STORAGEPORT --> SQL[SQLite Adapter]
    STORAGEPORT --> CLOUD[Cloud Sync Adapter - future]

    AIPORT --> LOCALAI[Local Model Adapter]
    AIPORT --> HOSTEDAI[Hosted Provider Adapters]

    INTPORT --> HEALTH[Health Adapters]
    INTPORT --> CAL[Calendar Adapters]
    INTPORT --> FILES[File/Blob Adapters]

    APP --> EVENTBUS[In-process Domain Events]
    EVENTBUS --> ANALYTICS[Progress/Aggregation Projectors]
    EVENTBUS --> OUTBOX[Sync Outbox - future]
```

title: Layer responsibilities
text: ### Layer responsibilities

title: Presentation
text:
#### Presentation

- routing and navigation,
- forms and validation feedback,
- dashboard widgets,
- local/offline/sync state presentation,
- permission and approval UX,
- no direct persistence calls outside approved repository/query hooks.

title: Application
text:
#### Application

- orchestrates use cases,
- enforces transaction boundaries,
- performs authorization/profile-scope checks,
- validates commands,
- coordinates AI proposals and approved writes,
- emits domain events.

title: Domain
text:
#### Domain

- entities/value objects,
- recurrence and scheduling rules,
- progress semantics,
- goal/task relationships,
- module rules,
- approval policy helpers,
- no framework/vendor imports.

title: Infrastructure/adapters
text:
#### Infrastructure/adapters

- IndexedDB,
- SQLite,
- secure credential APIs,
- AI provider SDK/HTTP,
- health/calendar APIs,
- file system/object storage,
- sync transport.

---

title: 4. Recommended repository structure
text:
## 4. Recommended repository structure

```text
omnivae/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/                      # Next.js app/PWA
│   └── mobile/                   # Capacitor config/native shells
├── packages/
│   ├── ui/                       # shared UI primitives/design tokens
│   ├── domain/                   # pure business entities/policies
│   ├── application/              # commands, queries, use cases
│   ├── storage/                  # storage ports + common repository contracts
│   ├── storage-indexeddb/        # web adapter
│   ├── storage-sqlite/           # mobile adapter
│   ├── crypto/                   # approved crypto/key abstractions
│   ├── ai/                       # provider-neutral AI contracts/orchestration
│   ├── ai-providers/             # optional provider adapters
│   ├── integrations/             # health/calendar/notifications ports
│   ├── sync/                     # outbox/conflict logic; later phases
│   ├── analytics/                # aggregation/projection logic
│   ├── config/                   # typed config and feature flags
│   └── test-support/             # factories/fixtures/harnesses
├── docs/
│   ├── prd.md
│   ├── architecture.md
│   ├── rules.md
│   ├── phases.md
│   ├── schema.md
│   ├── memory.md
│   └── testing.md
├── tests/
│   ├── integration/
│   ├── e2e/
│   ├── security/
│   └── fixtures/
└── README.md
```

Package names may be adjusted to workspace conventions, but boundaries must remain explicit.

---

title: 5. App launch and profile flow
text:
## 5. App launch and profile flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[App Launch] --> B{Existing profiles?}
    B -- No --> C[Create local profile / Guest]
    B -- Yes --> D[Profile chooser]
    C --> E[Configure local protection]
    D --> F[Unlock profile]
    E --> G[Onboarding / module choices]
    F --> H{Unlock successful?}
    H -- No --> F
    H -- Yes --> I[Load profile-scoped app context]
    G --> I
    I --> J[Dashboard]
    J --> K[Core/optional modules]
```

title: Profile boundary
text:
### Profile boundary

At runtime, the application obtains an explicit `ProfileContext` after successful local unlock. All profile-owned repositories require that context or derive it from an authenticated local session object.

Never design APIs like:

```ts
getTask(taskId)
```

when they can bypass scope. Prefer contracts conceptually equivalent to:

```ts
getTask(profileContext, taskId)
```

or repositories already constructed for a specific profile session.

The underlying store should still include `profile_id` constraints so isolation is enforced at more than one layer.

---

title: 6. Navigation/app flow
text:
## 6. Navigation/app flow

A default navigation model may expose:

```text
Dashboard
Calendar
Tasks
Goals
Notes
AI
More / Modules
  ├── Journal
  ├── Health
  ├── Study
  ├── Gym
  ├── Habits
  ├── Projects
  └── Files
Settings
```

Navigation is configuration-driven. Disabled optional modules must be removed or clearly inactive, not left as broken routes.

Tablet/desktop layouts may use persistent side navigation. Mobile may use bottom navigation for a small set of primary destinations plus a module launcher.

---

title: 7. Module architecture
text:
## 7. Module architecture

Each module should expose a small internal API and own its domain/application logic.

Example:

```text
Tasks Module
├── domain
│   ├── Task
│   ├── TaskStatus
│   └── TaskRecurrencePolicy
├── application
│   ├── CreateTask
│   ├── UpdateTask
│   ├── CompleteTask
│   └── QueryTasks
├── ports
│   └── TaskRepository
└── presentation
    ├── task-list
    └── task-editor
```

Cross-module integration must use stable domain references, application services, or domain events. Avoid one module reaching directly into another module's database tables from UI code.

---

title: 8. Core domain relationships
text:
## 8. Core domain relationships

```mermaid
erDiagram
    PROFILE ||--o{ TASK : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ GOAL : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ CALENDAR_EVENT : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ NOTE : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ JOURNAL_ENTRY : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ AI_CONVERSATION : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ HEALTH_SAMPLE : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ WORKOUT : owns
    PROFILE ||--o{ STUDY_SESSION : owns

    GOAL ||--o{ ENTITY_LINK : linked
    TASK ||--o{ ENTITY_LINK : linked
    NOTE ||--o{ ENTITY_LINK : linked
    CALENDAR_EVENT ||--o{ ENTITY_LINK : linked
```

Use explicit link entities for flexible cross-module relationships where a strict foreign key would create excessive coupling. Use direct foreign keys when ownership is unambiguous and stable.

---

title: 9. Storage abstraction
text: ## 9. Storage abstraction

title: Contract
text:
### Contract

Business/application logic must depend on repository/storage interfaces.

```text
Application use case
      ↓
Repository interface
      ↓
Storage unit-of-work / transaction abstraction
      ↓
IndexedDB adapter OR SQLite adapter
```

title: Required storage capabilities
text:
### Required storage capabilities

- profile-scoped CRUD,
- transactions or equivalent atomic groups,
- indexed queries by profile/time/status,
- schema version/migration support,
- soft-delete/tombstone support where sync requires it,
- change capture/outbox hook for future sync,
- attachment metadata references,
- deterministic test adapter/in-memory implementation where useful.

title: Do not
text:
### Do not

- scatter raw IndexedDB calls through React components,
- import SQLite libraries into domain code,
- let cloud sync become the only repository implementation,
- use browser `localStorage` for sensitive or structured primary data.

---

title: 10. Local database responsibilities
text:
## 10. Local database responsibilities

The local database stores personal domain records, not raw secret keys.

Stored locally:

- profile metadata that is safe to persist,
- tasks/calendar/goals/notes,
- journal/reflection,
- module records,
- AI conversations and memory according to user settings,
- integration metadata,
- local health/workout/study history,
- dashboard configuration,
- audit/provenance metadata as appropriate,
- sync metadata when enabled.

Stored in secure credential storage:

- AI API keys,
- OAuth refresh/access credentials where possible,
- encryption key material or wrapped keys according to the security design.

---

title: 11. Local security architecture
text:
## 11. Local security architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    AUTH[PIN/Password/Biometric] --> UNLOCK[Unlock Local Profile]
    UNLOCK --> KEY[Obtain/unwrap profile data key]
    KEY --> DB[(Profile-scoped encrypted/sensitive data)]
    KEY --> SESSION[In-memory profile session]
    SECURE[Platform secure storage / keychain] --> KEY
```

title: Rules
text:
### Rules

- Never implement custom cryptographic primitives.
- PIN/password must not be stored directly.
- Password-derived keys require an approved KDF with appropriate parameters.
- Biometrics should unlock protected key material through platform-supported APIs; biometric templates themselves are never handled by Omnivae.
- Lock/timeout behavior must clear sensitive in-memory state according to platform capabilities.

Exact algorithms/libraries require an explicit security decision before production hardening.

---

title: 12. Time architecture
text:
## 12. Time architecture

Store absolute timestamps in UTC/ISO or a robust native timestamp representation and preserve timezone information where local-date semantics matter.

Important distinctions:

- `created_at`: absolute instant,
- `due_at`: optional absolute instant,
- `scheduled_local_date`: may be needed for all-day/local-day semantics,
- `timezone`: IANA timezone when a schedule is timezone-bound,
- recurring templates: must define whether recurrence follows local wall-clock time.

Do not calculate week/month/year progress with naive UTC date truncation. Aggregation uses the profile's configured timezone unless the record has a domain-specific timezone.

---

title: 13. Calendar architecture
text: ## 13. Calendar architecture

title: Event model
text:
### Event model

Calendar events support:

- one-time timed events,
- all-day events,
- recurrence in later phases,
- local source,
- external source reference,
- template/provenance metadata,
- links to other entities.

title: Bulk schedule copy flow
text:
### Bulk schedule copy flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Select source day/week] --> B[Load source events/routines]
    B --> C[Choose destination dates/range]
    C --> D[Generate copy plan in memory]
    D --> E[Detect collisions / invalid dates]
    E --> F[Preview proposed changes]
    F --> G{User confirms?}
    G -- No --> H[Discard plan]
    G -- Yes --> I[Atomic write transaction]
    I --> J[Emit events / update projections]
```

The copy engine should work on normalized schedule items and date transforms rather than UI clones.

title: Bulk operation identity
text:
### Bulk operation identity

Records created by one copy/apply action should optionally carry a `bulk_operation_id` or provenance reference. This enables:

- undo where feasible,
- debugging,
- conflict inspection,
- test assertions.

---

title: 14. Notes-to-action architecture
text:
## 14. Notes-to-action architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    NOTE[Note] --> EXTRACT[User selects Convert]
    EXTRACT --> FORM[Pre-filled structured form]
    FORM --> CMD[Domain command]
    CMD --> NEW[Task/Event/Goal/etc.]
    NEW --> LINK[EntityLink to source note]
```

AI extraction may prefill fields later, but it must still flow through the same validated form/command path unless the user has explicitly approved an agent proposal.

---

title: 15. Progress/analytics architecture
text: ## 15. Progress/analytics architecture

title: Source of truth
text:
### Source of truth

```text
Task completions
Habit completions
Study sessions
Workout sessions/sets
Health samples
Goal evidence
Calendar/activity events
        ↓
Normalization
        ↓
Daily projections
        ↓
Weekly/monthly/yearly aggregation
```

Do not maintain independent manually-mutated counters as the only truth.

title: Projection strategy
text:
### Projection strategy

Early phases may compute on query for small datasets. As volume grows, introduce cached aggregate tables/materialized projections that are:

- versioned,
- invalidatable,
- rebuildable from source records,
- profile/timezone aware.

---

title: 16. AI architecture
text:
## 16. AI architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    UI[AI UI / Agent Request] --> ORCH[AI Orchestrator]
    ORCH --> CTX[Context Builder]
    CTX --> PERM[Permission & scope policy]
    PERM --> READS[Read-only domain tools]
    ORCH --> PROVIDER[AI Provider Port]
    PROVIDER --> LOCAL[Local Runtime Adapter]
    PROVIDER --> CLOUD[Hosted Provider Adapter]
    ORCH --> PARSE[Structured Response / Proposal Validator]
    PARSE --> PREVIEW[Proposal Preview]
    PREVIEW --> APPROVE{Approval required?}
    APPROVE -- Yes --> USER[User approval]
    USER --> COMMANDS[Validated domain commands]
    APPROVE -- No --> RESULT[Read-only answer]
    COMMANDS --> STORE[(Local Store)]
```

title: AI Provider Port
text:
### AI Provider Port

Conceptual capabilities:

```ts
interface AIProvider {
  validateConfiguration(...): Promise<ValidationResult>
  generateText(...): Promise<AIResponse>
  streamText?(...): AsyncIterable<AIChunk>
  supportsStructuredOutput(): boolean
  capabilities(): ProviderCapabilities
}
```

Provider-specific message formats must be translated at the adapter boundary.

title: Context builder
text:
### Context builder

The context builder must:

- use current profile only,
- obey module/memory/history permissions,
- include only data required for the task,
- tag provenance where useful,
- avoid sending secrets,
- avoid sending health/private context unless explicitly enabled for that request or policy.

---

title: 17. AI conversation and memory architecture
text:
## 17. AI conversation and memory architecture

Raw chats and durable memory are separate concepts.

```text
Conversation
├── messages
├── model/provider metadata
└── optional references

Memory
├── structured fact/preference/context
├── provenance
├── confidence/state
├── created/updated timestamps
└── retention/deletion state
```

A user may clear chats without necessarily clearing explicitly retained memory and vice versa, if the product UI offers both. The storage model must not make those operations impossible.

Memory retrieval is never cross-profile.

---

title: 18. Agent tool architecture
text:
## 18. Agent tool architecture

Agents do not get direct repository handles.

Expose narrow tools such as:

```text
read_tasks(filter)
read_calendar(range)
read_goals(status)
read_reflections(range, permission)
propose_tasks(...)
propose_calendar_changes(...)
apply_approved_proposal(proposal_id, approval_token)
```

title: Proposal object
text:
### Proposal object

A proposal should contain:

- proposal ID,
- profile ID internally,
