- requested intent,
- proposed operations,
- affected entities/date ranges,
- conflicts/warnings,
- human-readable explanation,
- creation/expiry timestamps,
- approval state,
- model/provider provenance.

Writes should be executed from validated proposal data, not by reparsing uncontrolled prose after approval.

---

title: 19. Nightly reflection architecture
text:
## 19. Nightly reflection architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    N[Reflection reminder/manual start] --> INPUT[Text/voice input]
    INPUT --> RAW[Save user narrative draft]
    RAW --> AI{AI enabled?}
    AI -- No --> SAVE[Save journal/reflection]
    AI -- Yes --> CONTEXT[Load allowed day context]
    CONTEXT --> SUMMARY[Generate summary + questions + proposals]
    SUMMARY --> REVIEW[User reviews]
    REVIEW --> CONFIRM{Confirm updates?}
    CONFIRM -- No --> SAVE
    CONFIRM -- Yes --> APPLY[Apply selected domain commands]
    APPLY --> SAVE
```

User-authored narrative and AI summary are stored separately. This preserves provenance and prevents the model from rewriting history.

---

title: 20. Health architecture
text:
## 20. Health architecture

Prefer a normalized health domain over vendor-specific fields.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    HC[Health Connect] --> ADAPTERS[Health Source Adapters]
    AH[Apple Health] --> ADAPTERS
    VENDOR[Vendor API/BLE] --> ADAPTERS
    MANUAL[Manual Input] --> NORM[Normalizer]
    ADAPTERS --> NORM
    NORM --> HS[(Health Samples)]
    HS --> DEDUPE[Deduplication / source rules]
    DEDUPE --> DASH[Health Dashboard]
    DEDUPE --> INSIGHTS[Local analytics / opt-in AI]
```

title: Health sample normalization
text:
### Health sample normalization

Common normalized fields:

- metric type,
- numeric/value payload,
- unit,
- start/end timestamp,
- source/provider,
- source record ID,
- device metadata if permitted,
- quality/confidence metadata if available.

Do not coerce incompatible vendor concepts into false equivalence.

title: Import safety
text:
### Import safety

- track source IDs to avoid duplicates,
- preserve original source metadata,
- support revocation/disconnect behavior,
- never infer a metric that the source did not provide,
- do not upload health history to an AI provider by default.

---

title: 21. Files/attachments architecture
text:
## 21. Files/attachments architecture

Store binary files behind a file/blob abstraction.

```text
FileMetadata
  ├── id
  ├── profile_id
  ├── storage_provider
  ├── storage_locator
  ├── mime_type
  ├── size
  ├── checksum (when appropriate)
  └── lifecycle state
```

Domain entities reference metadata IDs. The UI must not assume every attachment is a web URL.

Web may use browser storage APIs; mobile may use app-private filesystem storage. Future cloud sync can map the same metadata to object storage.

---

title: 22. Integration architecture
text:
## 22. Integration architecture

All external integrations use adapters with explicit capability boundaries.

title: Calendar port
text:
### Calendar port

Conceptual operations:

- list external calendars,
- request authorization,
- pull events for a range,
- map external event IDs,
- push approved writes only where supported,
- revoke/disconnect.

title: Health port
text:
### Health port

- request permissions for selected metric types,
- query changed records/ranges,
- normalize source data,
- store source cursors/tokens safely,
- revoke/disconnect.

title: Notification port
text:
### Notification port

- request permission,
- schedule local notification,
- cancel local notification,
- list app-owned schedules where supported.

---

title: 23. Sync architecture — future
text:
## 23. Sync architecture — future

Sync is intentionally a later layer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DB[(Local DB)] --> CHANGE[Change capture]
    CHANGE --> OUTBOX[(Outbox)]
    OUTBOX --> ENGINE[Sync Engine]
    ENGINE --> REMOTE[Remote Store]
    REMOTE --> ENGINE
    ENGINE --> INBOX[Incoming changes]
    INBOX --> CONFLICT[Conflict resolver]
    CONFLICT --> DB
```

title: Required sync metadata
text:
### Required sync metadata

At minimum, synced entities need semantics for:

- stable global/local ID,
- version or revision,
- `updated_at`,
- deleted/tombstone state,
- origin/device ID where useful,
- sync state,
- remote revision token if provider exposes one.

title: Conflict strategy
text:
### Conflict strategy

Do not default every entity to last-write-wins without analysis.

Possible per-entity policies:

- immutable event append/merge,
- field-level merge,
- explicit conflict UI,
- server-authoritative metadata,
- latest-write for low-risk preferences.

Conflict policies must be documented in `schema.md`/ADR before sync ships.

---

title: 24. Optional cloud architecture
text:
## 24. Optional cloud architecture

When managed cloud is introduced:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    CLIENT[Omnivae Clients] --> EDGE[CDN/WAF]
    EDGE --> WEB[Web/API Layer]
    WEB --> AUTH[Authentication]
    WEB --> API[Authorized Application API]
    API --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    API --> OBJ[(Object Storage)]
    API --> CACHE[(Redis - only if useful)]
    API --> WORKER[Background Workers - only when needed]
```

Security requirements:

- authenticated session determines user identity,
- never trust client-provided owner IDs,
- row/user authorization on every protected operation,
- RLS where suitable,
- secure secret management,
- rate limits/abuse controls,
- backups and tested restore procedures,
- export/deletion support,
- audit logs for security-relevant actions.

---

title: 25. Data ownership modes
text: ## 25. Data ownership modes

title: Mode A — Local only
text:
### Mode A — Local only

```text
Device → local profile → encrypted/protected local data
```

No managed Omnivae account required.

title: Mode B — User-owned cloud/backup
text:
### Mode B — User-owned cloud/backup

```text
Local data → encrypted export/sync package → user's chosen storage
```

This requires a format/versioning design before implementation.

title: Mode C — Managed Omnivae cloud
text:
### Mode C — Managed Omnivae cloud

```text
Local-first client ↔ authenticated sync API ↔ managed data services
```

Managed cloud must not erase local-first semantics.

---

title: 26. Error and resilience architecture
text:
## 26. Error and resilience architecture

Every external action must have a typed failure path.

Examples:

- AI provider unavailable,
- API key invalid,
- permission revoked,
- health source partially unavailable,
- calendar write rejected,
- local storage quota exceeded,
- migration failed,
- sync conflict,
- offline state.

Rules:

- never silently discard user input,
- use local drafts for long-form input where practical,
- transactions roll back partial bulk writes,
- retry only idempotent/safely retryable operations,
- surface recovery actions to the user.

---

title: 27. Observability
text:
## 27. Observability

Local-first does not mean no diagnostics. It means diagnostics must respect privacy.

Allowed patterns:

- local structured logs with redaction,
- crash/error reports only with clear privacy controls if remote telemetry is later added,
- performance metrics without message contents/secrets,
- correlation IDs that are not secret identifiers.

Never log:

- API keys,
- passwords/PINs,
- encryption keys,
- raw health payloads by default,
- raw journal/AI conversation content by default,
- full OAuth tokens.

---

title: 28. Feature flags and migrations
text:
## 28. Feature flags and migrations

Use typed feature flags for incomplete/incremental capabilities. A flag must not be used to hide failing required functionality in a release declared complete.

Database migrations must be:

- versioned,
- deterministic,
- covered by upgrade tests,
- reversible where practical or accompanied by a safe forward-only recovery path,
- tested against representative older fixtures.

Never delete user data in a migration without an explicit product/data migration decision.

---

title: 29. Testing seams
text:
## 29. Testing seams

Architecture must make the following easy to test:

- domain rules without a browser,
- application use cases against in-memory/fake repositories,
- identical repository conformance tests against IndexedDB and SQLite,
- AI orchestration with fake providers,
- agent approval without live LLM calls,
- health/calendar adapters with fixtures,
- offline flows,
- migration upgrades,
- profile isolation,
- bulk calendar operations atomically.

If a design makes these impractical, revisit the design before implementation.

---

title: 30. Key sequence diagrams
text: ## 30. Key sequence diagrams

title: 30.1 Create task offline
text:
### 30.1 Create task offline

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant UI as UI
    participant A as CreateTask use case
    participant R as TaskRepository
    participant DB as Local DB
    U->>UI: Enter task
    UI->>A: CreateTaskCommand
    A->>A: Validate + profile scope
    A->>R: save(task)
    R->>DB: transaction write
    DB-->>R: committed
    R-->>A: task
    A-->>UI: success
```

title: 30.2 AI proposes a schedule
text:
### 30.2 AI proposes a schedule

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant AI as AI Orchestrator
    participant T as Read Tools
    participant P as Provider
    participant V as Proposal Validator
    participant W as Domain Commands
    U->>AI: "Plan my week"
    AI->>T: Read allowed goals/tasks/calendar
    T-->>AI: scoped context
    AI->>P: Generate structured proposal
    P-->>AI: model output
    AI->>V: validate/normalize
    V-->>U: preview + conflicts
    U->>AI: approve selected changes
    AI->>W: apply approved operations
    W-->>U: committed result
```

title: 30.3 Cross-profile access rejection
text:
### 30.3 Cross-profile access rejection

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as Profile A UI
    participant APP as Application
    participant REPO as Repository
    UI->>APP: Request entity owned by Profile B
    APP->>REPO: scoped query(Profile A, entity id)
    REPO-->>APP: not found / forbidden
    APP-->>UI: safe error
```

title: 31. Architecture decisions already locked
text:
## 31. Architecture decisions already locked

These are the current baseline:

- Product name: **Omnivae**.
- Product category: personal intelligence / life operating system.
- Local-first and privacy-first.
- Multiple isolated local profiles.
- Job/Career is optional.
- Provider-agnostic BYOK AI.
- AI chat local by default.
- Explicit chat deletion/history controls.
- Controlled agents; preview/approval before consequential writes.
- Storage abstraction between domain logic and platform database.
- Next.js + React web/PWA baseline.
- Capacitor mobile wrapper baseline.
- IndexedDB web adapter.
- SQLite mobile adapter.
- Modular monolith initially.
- Optional future sync/cloud.
- Stable IDs for sync readiness.
- UTC/robust timestamps plus timezone-aware local semantics.
- Progress intelligence is the long-term AI differentiator.

---

title: 32. Architecture decisions still open
text:
## 32. Architecture decisions still open

Do not guess these in production code:

- exact monorepo tooling,
- exact client state/query library,
- exact IndexedDB wrapper,
- exact SQLite library/plugin,
- exact local encryption implementation,
- exact secure-storage plugin,
- exact rich-text editor,
- exact charting library,
- exact recurrence library,
- exact AI provider list for first release,
- exact health integration order,
- exact cloud vendor/backend framework,
- exact sync conflict policy per entity,
- exact object storage layout,
- exact local search/indexing engine.

For low-risk library choices needed to proceed, an agent may choose a mature dependency consistent with `rules.md`, document it in `memory.md`, and add an ADR when it meaningfully constrains architecture.

---

title: 33. Forbidden architecture shortcuts
text:
## 33. Forbidden architecture shortcuts

Do not:

- use one global unscoped user-data repository,
- store API keys in `localStorage`, source, logs, URLs, or analytics,
- call external AI directly from every feature,
- let an LLM execute SQL or arbitrary repository mutations,
- couple domain types to provider response schemas,
- make cloud availability required for local CRUD,
- mark AI-generated progress as fact without evidence/user confirmation,
- duplicate daily/weekly/monthly/yearly tracking tables as separate truths,
- add microservices just to look scalable,
- implement custom crypto,
- silently change architectural decisions while coding.

---

title: 34. Architecture completion checklist
text:
## 34. Architecture completion checklist

Before a feature is considered architecture-compliant, verify:

- [ ] Domain/application logic is not tied to a platform database.
- [ ] Every personal record is profile-scoped.
- [ ] Offline/local behavior is defined.
- [ ] Secret handling is explicit.
- [ ] Cross-module relationships use approved interfaces/references.
- [ ] AI context and writes follow permission/approval rules.
- [ ] New source records support future aggregation/sync where relevant.
- [ ] Failure behavior is defined.
- [ ] Tests can exercise the feature without a live external service.
- [ ] Required tests in `testing.md` pass.

The checkbox may only be marked after the corresponding test evidence exists.

title: AI implementation decision — 2026-10-04
text:
## AI implementation decision — 2026-10-04

Hosted adapters receive prompt/context and an abort signal, never storage handles. Provider output is strictly parsed into an allowlisted command shape, then normalized and domain-validated before encrypted proposal storage. Approval binds exact SHA-256/version and checks all scoped source revisions before a single transaction. Follow-up revisions invalidate prior approvals. Unsupported destructive commands fail closed. All writes and generated task history are part of the previewed proposal. Full product controls/memory/voice/on-device remain required.

title: 2026-10-06 — Standalone inference decision
text:
## 2026-10-06 — Standalone inference decision
Native LiteRT-LM 0.17.1 is added behind the AIProvider port. Public imported weights are device-shared; each request uses a fresh native conversation, with no storage/tool access. User data stays in profile-scoped encrypted application services. Android on-device speech recognition and offline-only TTS are separate capabilities, explicitly unavailable when absent. No cloud fallback. See docs/offline-ai.md for constraints and pending gates.

title: Omnivae — Backend and Data Structure
text:
# Omnivae — Backend and Data Structure

> Status: Logical schema contract  
> Version: 1.0  
> Last consolidated: 2026-09-08  
> Applies to: local stores first; future cloud mappings second

title: 0. Purpose
text:
## 0. Purpose

This document defines the **logical data model** for Omnivae. It is deliberately storage-engine-neutral so the same domain model can map to IndexedDB on web, SQLite on mobile, and a future PostgreSQL-backed sync service.

This is not permission to create all future tables on day one. Implement tables/stores by phase, but preserve the contracts and invariants below.

Any material schema change requires:

1. migration/version change,
2. migration tests,
3. update to this file,
4. update to `memory.md`,
5. passing tests before the related task is marked complete.

---

title: 1. Global schema principles
text: ## 1. Global schema principles

title: 1.1 Stable IDs
text:
### 1.1 Stable IDs

Use UUID/ULID-class stable IDs for user-domain records. IDs must not encode sensitive data.

Conceptual type:

```text
EntityId = opaque string, globally collision-resistant
```

title: 1.2 Profile ownership
text:
### 1.2 Profile ownership

Every personal record must be directly or transitively owned by a `profile_id`.

Prefer direct `profile_id` on frequently queried personal tables even if ownership can be inferred through a parent. This improves isolation checks and indexing.

title: 1.3 Common timestamps
text:
### 1.3 Common timestamps

Unless a table is immutable and clearly documented otherwise, use:

```text
created_at      UTC timestamp
updated_at      UTC timestamp
```

When deletion must synchronize or remain recoverable:

```text
deleted_at      nullable UTC timestamp
```

title: 1.4 Sync-ready metadata
text:
### 1.4 Sync-ready metadata

Do not require sync fields in every MVP table if sync is not yet implemented, but reserve the model for:

```text
revision             integer/string
origin_device_id     nullable ID
sync_state            local_only | pending | synced | conflict | error
remote_revision      nullable string
last_synced_at        nullable timestamp
```

title: 1.5 Provenance
text:
### 1.5 Provenance

Where AI, import, conversion, or bulk operations can create records, preserve source/provenance:

```text
created_by_type      user | ai_approved | import | system | sync
created_by_ref       nullable ID/string
source_type          nullable enum
source_id            nullable ID/string
bulk_operation_id    nullable ID
```

title: 1.6 Secrets
text:
### 1.6 Secrets

**Do not store plaintext credentials in this logical database.** Store only a reference to secure credential storage.

---

title: 2. Value conventions
text: ## 2. Value conventions

title: IDs
text:
### IDs

```text
profile_id, task_id, etc. = opaque stable ID
```

title: Timestamps
text:
### Timestamps

```text
UTC instant: 2026-09-08T12:34:56.789Z
```

title: Local date
text:
### Local date

For date-only semantics:

```text
YYYY-MM-DD
```

title: Timezone
text:
### Timezone

Use IANA names:

```text
Asia/Kolkata
America/New_York
```

title: JSON
text:
### JSON

Use structured JSON only for extensible metadata that is not heavily queried. Do not hide core query fields inside one JSON blob.

title: 28. Deletion semantics
text:
# 28. Deletion semantics

Every entity must declare one of:

title: Hard delete
text:
### Hard delete

Use only when safe and no sync/audit/recovery semantics require retention.

title: Soft delete
text:
### Soft delete

Set `deleted_at`, hide from ordinary queries, allow purge later.

title: Tombstone
text:
### Tombstone

For sync, retain minimal deletion identity/version until remote peers acknowledge deletion.

title: Cascade rules
text:
### Cascade rules

Do not cascade-delete meaningful independent records merely because a link is deleted.

Examples:

- deleting a note does not automatically delete a task created from it,
- deleting an entity link never deletes either endpoint,
- deleting a dashboard widget does not delete source module data,
- deleting a calendar template does not necessarily delete already created events.

Each implementation must test its chosen behavior.

---

title: 29. Referential integrity rules
text:
# 29. Referential integrity rules

Even when IndexedDB cannot enforce SQL foreign keys directly, application/repository logic must enforce equivalent invariants.

Required checks:

- linked entities exist,
- linked entities share profile ownership,
- parent IDs cannot create cycles where hierarchy forbids them,
- deleted parents follow documented orphan behavior,
- external source IDs remain unique within appropriate provider/profile scope.

SQLite/PostgreSQL implementations should use foreign keys where practical in addition to application checks.

---

title: 30. Indexing plan
text:
# 30. Indexing plan

At minimum, index common query dimensions:

- `profile_id`,
- status,
- local date/time range,
- `updated_at`,
- foreign relationship IDs,
- external source IDs,
- sync state,
- proposal status,
- AI conversation ID.

Do not add indexes speculatively to every field. Use query patterns and profiling.

title: 31. Data encryption classification
text:
# 31. Data encryption classification

Classify data at least conceptually:

title: Class S — secrets
text:
### Class S — secrets

- API keys,
- OAuth tokens,
- encryption keys,
- password/PIN credential material.

Storage: secure credential store / protected keychain; not ordinary app DB.

title: Class H — highly private
text:
### Class H — highly private

- journal/reflections,
- AI conversations/memory,
- health data,
- potentially sensitive notes/files.

Storage: local protected/encrypted strategy; external sharing is opt-in/contextual.

title: Class P — personal operational
text:
### Class P — personal operational

- tasks,
- calendar,
- goals,
- study/gym/habits.

Storage: profile-scoped local DB, protected according to app security design.

title: Class C — configuration/non-sensitive
text:
### Class C — configuration/non-sensitive

- widget positions,
- module enabled flags,
- safe UI preferences.

Still profile-scoped if user-specific.

# 32. Schema migration model

Maintain a monotonically increasing local schema version.

Conceptual migration directory:

```text
migrations/
  0001_profiles.ts
  0002_tasks_goals_notes.ts
  0003_calendar.ts
  0004_dashboard.ts
  ...
```

Each migration includes:

- `from_version`,
- `to_version`,
- migration operation,
- data transformation,
- validation,
- test fixtures.

title: Required migration tests

### Required migration tests

- fresh install,
- previous version with empty tables,
- previous version with representative data,
- multiple profiles,
- deleted records where applicable,
- failed/interrupted migration recovery behavior.

# 33. Cloud schema mapping — future

When PostgreSQL exists, do not simply copy every local implementation detail blindly.

Cloud tables should preserve domain semantics while adding:

- authenticated account ownership,
- device/sync metadata,
- authorization policies/RLS,
- audit fields,
- remote revision/version,
- server timestamps where required.

The server derives account identity from the authenticated session. The client cannot choose another owner's identity by supplying `user_id`.

text:
# 36. Schema acceptance checklist for new entities

Before adding a new entity/table/store, answer:

- [ ] What is the owner/profile boundary?
- [ ] Is the ID stable enough for future sync?
- [ ] What are create/update/delete semantics?
- [ ] What timestamps are required?
- [ ] Does it contain secrets? If yes, why is it not in secure storage?
- [ ] Is it source data or derived data?
- [ ] What indexes support real queries?
- [ ] What links/foreign keys are required?
- [ ] What happens when linked records are deleted?
- [ ] What is offline behavior?
- [ ] What migration introduces it?
- [ ] What tests verify it?
- [ ] Are AI/import provenance fields needed?
- [ ] Will future sync need tombstones/versioning?

Do not mark schema work complete until all required schema and migration tests pass.

title: Implementation draft — local profiles, schema version 1 (2026-09-28)
text:
## Implementation draft — local profiles, schema version 1 (2026-09-28)

Status: prototype, disabled in shipped UI; no migration or feature completion claim.

The initial adapters implement profiles, profile_auth and encrypted profile_settings. TypeScript serialization uses camelCase for the fields implemented so far; SQLite maps these to snake_case columns. Remaining logical fields (including full profile lifecycle and complete settings) must be reconciled before the phase gate; these prototypes do not replace the logical contract above.

IndexedDB migration 0001 creates three stores atomically. The current test verifies fresh initialization and populated reopen; it does NOT prove an older populated schema upgrade. SQLite initializes its version-1 tables with parameterized queries and an atomic multi-insert for profile creation. Native conformance and interrupted-migration cases remain pending.

Authentication stores a random salt, PBKDF2 iteration count, wrapped profile data key and throttling state. AES-GCM encrypted preferences are bound to profile identity through authenticated additional data. Neither passwords nor unwrapped keys are stored. Native chooser metadata remains unencrypted; the preference payload is encrypted at the application boundary. See docs/adr-002-profile-security.md.

## Implementation migrations 0002/0003 — profiles and core planning (2026-10-03)

Status: in_progress; full logical schema and phase gates are not yet complete.

- Version 2 adds standard profile type and active lifecycle metadata to version-1 profiles. Public chooser identity remains unencrypted. Existing wrapped keys and preferences ciphertext are preserved. New preference defaults are applied after decryption (memory capture and health AI access remain off). Runtime lock is a session condition, not a persistent lifecycle value.
- Version 3 creates an encrypted per-record `records` store/table keyed by (profile_id, id), with profile index (and native kind index), revision, kind and ciphertext envelope. Logical task/goal/note/calendar/milestone/task-event/journal fields are serialized in authenticated encrypted payloads; application services enforce their invariants. This physical mapping preserves the logical entities above; it does not claim the remaining entities are implemented.
- AES-GCM authenticated context includes profile, record ID and revision. Search currently decrypts only the active profile's records locally; future performance work must preserve this boundary.
- Multi-record writes compare the read snapshot and changed-record revisions inside the transaction, then commit atomically. A concurrent edit causes a recoverable conflict instead of lost updates or dangling cross-record links.
- Deletion writes a tombstone and atomically clears optional links; deleting a goal tombstones its owned milestones but preserves independent tasks/child goals. Task transition history remains; derived progress excludes deleted records.
- All-day event end dates are exclusive. Timed event instants are stored as UTC ISO strings with an IANA timezone. Nonexistent wall times are rejected; repeated times require an explicit earlier/later choice.
- IndexedDB version-change transactions and native plugin upgrade statements preserve existing data. Native upgrade tests and crash/failure recovery remain mandatory before migration completion.

- Dashboard preferences now include ordered visible widget keys and Journal module visibility in encrypted settings; old preference payloads receive non-destructive defaults on read. Source-based task/calendar/journal range summaries use profile timezone and configurable week start. This is the initial implemented dashboard subset, not all P3 widgets/modules.

title: Timed goal targets — 2026-10-04 additive payload extension
text:
### Timed goal targets — 2026-10-04 additive payload extension

Encrypted goal payloads may include targetAt (UTC instant) and timezone (IANA zone); targetDate remains date-only. targetDate and targetAt are mutually exclusive. Timed targets require timezone. Old records without either new field remain valid; no table migration is needed because the version 3 record envelope is unchanged. UI interprets edits in active profile timezone and shows that timezone explicitly. Task dueAt and scheduled start/end retain existing semantics. Common createdAt/updatedAt values are service-managed and now visible in task/goal cards.

title: AI proposal record payloads — 2026-10-04
text:
### AI proposal record payloads — 2026-10-04

Version 3 encrypted record envelopes now carry ai_proposal and ai_approval kinds, mapping logical ai_proposals/ai_proposal_approvals. Proposal payload stores typed before/after operations, derived task events, provider/model, intent, warnings, scoped base revisions, expiry, content SHA-256, monotonically increasing proposalVersion and state. Approval stores exact version/hash and all selected record IDs. Full-plan approval is supported; partial approval and destructive AI operations are not yet supported and are rejected. Plan application and durable task events/approval/proposal state are one atomic snapshot-checked transaction. Profile isolation applies below presentation; these payloads never contain provider credentials. Existing records need no table rewrite.

title: Appearance persistence migration 0004 — 2026-10-04
text:
## Appearance persistence migration 0004 — 2026-10-04
- IndexedDB version 4 adds profile_backgrounds keyed by profileId. SQLite version 4 adds profile_backgrounds(profile_id PK/FK profiles, encrypted_value). Each holds one bounded encrypted raster asset per profile; preferences and planning records never embed image bytes. Replacement/removal is a single atomic storage operation. No prior data is rewritten.
- Encrypted preference payload appearanceVersion 2 adds accentColor/backgroundColor, validated #RRGGBB. Older payloads receive version 2 defaults after decryption without overwriting existing settings.
- Backgrounds use the existing AES-GCM adapter with profile-specific :background authenticated context. UI reads through token-authorized ProfileService methods. Browser platform adapter decodes/re-encodes raster content, strips metadata, bounds input at 12 MB/40 MP and output at 1920 pixels/1.4 million data-URL characters. This is an appearance asset implementation, not completion of the general Files module.

title: Section navigation payloads — 2026-10-04
text:
## Section navigation payloads — 2026-10-04
- Existing v4 generic encrypted records support new discriminants custom_section and section_entry, payloadVersion 1. A section has title, description and archived; an entry has sectionId, title, content and completed. Both preserve profileId, id, revision, timestamps and deletion tombstones. SectionService enforces scope, same-profile live section links and compare-and-swap writes. Hiding uses archived and preserves entries; entry deletion is tombstoned only after user confirmation. No physical schema change beyond migration 0004.
- Preference navigationVersion 1 adds sectionLabels (built-in key to name) and sectionOrder (built-in keys/custom:<UUID>). Legacy ciphertext receives non-destructive defaults after unlock. enabledModules/journalEnabled remain visibility controls for built-ins.

title: Calendar gallery and preference additions — 2026-10-05
text:
## Calendar gallery and preference additions — 2026-10-05
Storage migration 0005 adds calendar_gallery, one encrypted bounded snapshot per profile, containing version 1, selectedId, activeId, and up to six validated resized raster assets. Ciphertext binds to profile-id:calendar-gallery. Writes compare previous IV transactionally to reject stale updates. Profile deletion transaction removes all five child stores/tables then identity. Original device image files remain untouched.
Preferences add sectionStyles keyed by stable built-in/custom section identity, dashboardCharts keyed by widget, and calendarDisplay (imageTransparency 0..100, font enum, fontColor #RRGGBB). Legacy decrypted preferences receive defaults; no credentials or image data are placed in preferences.

title: 0. How to use this plan

## 0. How to use this plan

This document defines implementation sequence and gates. It is written for AGY/coding agents so work can continue across sessions without losing architectural intent.

For each phase:

1. Read the relevant PRD sections.
2. Read architecture/schema constraints.
3. Implement only the phase scope plus necessary seams.
4. Add tests as defined in `testing.md`.
5. Run the phase gate.
6. Update `memory.md` with exact test evidence.
7. Mark the phase complete only if every required gate passes.

- `not_started`
- `in_progress`
- `implemented_unverified`
- `blocked`
- `failed_tests`
- `completed`

# Final implementation instruction

The roadmap is intentionally staged so that Omnivae becomes a reliable local personal system before it becomes an AI-heavy cloud product.

An agent must not skip foundational correctness because a later AI feature is more exciting. Data integrity, profile isolation, offline behavior, and tests are prerequisites for trustworthy intelligence.

title: Omnivae — Feature Testing and Completion Contract
text:
# Omnivae — Feature Testing and Completion Contract

> Status: Binding QA/completion source of truth  
> Version: 1.0  
> Last consolidated: 2026-09-08  
> Audience: AGY/coding agents, QA, reviewers

title: 0. Absolute completion rule
text:
# 0. Absolute completion rule

**NEVER mark a task, subtask, feature, bug, refactor, migration, phase, or release as completed unless ALL test cases required for that scope pass.**

There is no “mostly complete” exception.

If implementation exists but one required test fails, the correct status is:

- `failed_tests`, or
- `implemented_unverified` if the test cannot yet be executed.

If a required test is skipped, quarantined, disabled, or blocked, the work is **not completed**.

A visual check alone is not sufficient when automated or reproducible tests are required.

---

title: 1. Purpose
text:
# 1. Purpose

This document defines:

- test layers,
- required test categories,
- feature-specific test cases,
- phase gates,
- regression expectations,
- evidence required before completion,
- rules for failed/flaky/blocked tests.

AGY must use this document as a completion state machine, not merely as a testing suggestion list.

---

title: 2. Status state machine
text:
# 2. Status state machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> not_started
    not_started --> in_progress
    in_progress --> implemented_unverified
    implemented_unverified --> failed_tests: any required test fails
    implemented_unverified --> blocked: required test cannot run
    failed_tests --> in_progress: fixing
    blocked --> in_progress: blocker resolved
    in_progress --> ready_for_verification
    ready_for_verification --> failed_tests: any required test fails
    ready_for_verification --> completed: ALL required tests pass
    completed --> in_progress: behavior changes or regression discovered
```

title: Rule
text:
### Rule

`completed` is a **test-derived state**, not an agent opinion.

title: 34. Security regression suite
text:
# 34. Security regression suite

Run for any release touching auth, storage, AI, files, sync, or integrations.

Minimum suite:

- `SEC-ISOLATION-*`
- API key secret tests,
- approval bypass tests,
- export profile-scope test,
- attachment access test,
- health permission tests if health changed,
- cloud authorization tests if cloud changed.

Add automated checks for:

- XSS/sanitization where rich content exists,
- CSRF/session security where server mutations exist,
- unsafe URL schemes in links/attachments,
- path traversal in file adapters,
- SQL/query injection in server/storage layers,
- dependency vulnerabilities according to release policy.

---

title: 35. Offline regression suite
text:
# 35. Offline regression suite

Run for changes touching core local modules/storage/service worker/mobile shell.

Required user flows:

1. launch/unlock local profile offline,
2. dashboard renders local data,
3. create/edit/complete task,
4. create/edit note,
5. create/edit local calendar event,
6. journal entry save,
7. study/workout/habit save if modules shipped,
8. existing AI chat history view,
9. local AI works if configured,
10. external-only actions show unavailable/queued state rather than false success.

---

title: 36. Migration regression suite
text:
# 36. Migration regression suite

For every release with schema changes:

- fresh latest DB,
- upgrade from immediately previous release,
- upgrade from oldest supported release/fixture,
- multiple profiles,
- representative records from all touched modules,
- deleted/archived records,
- AI history/memory if schema changed,
- file metadata if schema changed,
- failure recovery behavior.

A successful fresh install does **not** prove migration completion.

---

title: 37. Accessibility regression suite
text:
# 37. Accessibility regression suite

At least for core flows changed:

- keyboard reachability,
- visible focus,
- labels/accessible names,
- modal/dialog focus management,
- destructive confirmation semantics,
- no status conveyed by color alone,
- mobile touch targets,
- responsive no-horizontal-overflow where not intentional.

Automated accessibility tools are useful but do not replace manual smoke checks for important flows.

---

title: 38. Performance tests
text:
# 38. Performance tests

Define numeric budgets as implementation matures. At minimum test representative data volumes for:

- task/calendar list queries,
- dashboard aggregation,
- notes search,
- AI conversation history pagination,
- health sample range queries,
- large health import,
- bulk schedule plan/commit,
- app startup/offline startup.

A performance optimization cannot change correctness semantics; regression tests remain required.

---

title: 39. Test data rules
text:
# 39. Test data rules

- Use synthetic/non-sensitive fixtures.
- Never place real API keys in fixtures.
- Create at least two profiles for privacy tests.
- Include timezone fixtures such as a non-DST timezone and a DST timezone.
- Include leap-year dates.
- Include empty, normal, and boundary-sized datasets.
- Health fixtures must clearly label source/provider/unit.
- AI fixtures should be deterministic; fake providers should return known structured outputs.

---

title: 40. Mocking rules
text:
# 40. Mocking rules

Mock external boundaries, not the core behavior being tested.

Good:

- fake AI provider returns proposal JSON while real proposal validator/application command runs,
- health provider fixture feeds real normalizer/dedupe,
- fake clock tests recurrence/time boundaries.

Bad:

- mocking repository success in a test whose purpose is transaction atomicity,
- mocking approval validator in a test whose purpose is approval enforcement,
- mocking profile filter in an isolation test.

---

title: 41. Flaky test policy
text:
# 41. Flaky test policy

A flaky required test blocks trustworthy completion until addressed.

Process:

1. reproduce with repeated runs,
2. identify nondeterminism,
3. fix test or underlying race,
4. document cause,
5. rerun required suite.

Do not simply add retries to conceal a real race.

If a test is genuinely environment-dependent and temporarily blocked, status remains `blocked`, not completed.

---

title: 42. Failed test policy
text:
# 42. Failed test policy

When any required test fails:

```text
feature_status = failed_tests
```

Then:

1. capture failing test ID/name,
2. capture essential error,
3. determine whether code or expectation violates source-of-truth docs,
4. fix correct layer,
5. rerun focused case,
6. rerun scope suite,
7. rerun regression gate,
8. update `memory.md`.

Do not change the test expectation merely to match broken output.

---

title: 43. Skipped/quarantined test policy
text:
# 43. Skipped/quarantined test policy

A required test that is skipped/quarantined counts as **not passed**.

Allowed reasons to skip only if the feature is not claiming completion for that scope, e.g.:

- provider integration not implemented yet,
- mobile-only adapter unavailable in current early phase.

If the feature/release claims that capability, the corresponding test cannot remain skipped.

---

title: 44. Manual test policy
text:
# 44. Manual test policy

Some platform behaviors require manual verification, for example:

- biometrics on real device,
- OS notification interaction,
- health permission UX,
- stylus feel,
- accessibility screen reader behavior,
- mobile background behavior.

Manual required cases need recorded evidence:

```text
Test ID
Device/OS/browser
Build/commit
Steps
Expected
Actual
PASS/FAIL
Date
Tester/agent if applicable
```

A required manual test marked “not run” blocks completion.

---

title: 45. Feature completion manifest
text:
# 45. Feature completion manifest

For every feature completed, AGY should record in `memory.md`:

```markdown
### Completion evidence — <feature>
- Status: completed
- Acceptance criteria: all satisfied
- Required test IDs: <range/list>
- Unit: PASS (<count>)
- Integration: PASS (<count>)
- E2E: PASS (<count>)
- Security/privacy: PASS (<count or n/a reason>)
- Offline: PASS (<count or n/a reason>)
- Migration: PASS (<count or n/a reason>)
- Static/type/lint: PASS
- Manual: PASS/N/A with rationale
- Skipped required tests: 0
- Failing required tests: 0
- Build/commit: <id if available>
```

If `Skipped required tests > 0` or `Failing required tests > 0`, status cannot be completed.

---

title: 46. Subtask completion rule
text:
# 46. Subtask completion rule

The absolute rule applies even to subtasks.

Example task:

```text
Feature: Copy day schedule
Subtasks:
A. date transformation engine
B. conflict detector
C. preview UI
D. atomic commit
E. E2E flow
```

Subtask A can be completed only after all tests assigned to A pass. The parent feature can be completed only after A-E and the cross-feature/regression tests pass.

Do not mark parent complete because every coding subtask is “implemented” if E2E/security/regression tests still fail.

---

title: 47. Phase completion algorithm for AGY
text:
# 47. Phase completion algorithm for AGY

Use this exact logic conceptually:

```text
required = collect_required_tests(phase, shipped_scope)
results = run(required)

if any(result == FAIL for result in results):
    phase.status = failed_tests
elif any(result in [NOT_RUN, BLOCKED, SKIPPED] for result in results):
    phase.status = implemented_unverified_or_blocked
else:
    phase.status = completed
```

There is no percentage threshold.

---

text:
# 50. Final instruction to AGY

The point of testing Omnivae is not to maximize green checkmarks. It is to protect a private, local-first system that may contain a user's plans, reflections, health history, and AI context.

Therefore:

- test the boundary, not just the happy path,
- test two profiles,
- test offline,
- test deletion,
- test migrations,
- test approval bypass,
- test date/time edges,
- test imported data provenance,

Capacitor mobile wrappers

Application/domain layer

Storage abstraction

- UTC/robust timestamps plus timezone-aware local semantics,
- domain logic does not import platform storage APIs,

title: R1 — Feature sprawl

## R1 — Feature sprawl

Omnivae can easily become ten apps at once. Preserve phase order and modularity.

title: R2 — AI before reliable data

## R2 — AI before reliable data

Building advanced agents before tasks/calendar/reflection/history are reliable produces shallow intelligence. Capture trustworthy source data first.

title: R3 — Cross-profile leakage
text:
## R3 — Cross-profile leakage

One unscoped repository/search/cache can violate the central privacy promise. Isolation tests are mandatory.

title: R4 — Cloud-first drift

## R4 — Cloud-first drift

Adding auth/sync too early may make offline/local mode second-class. Prevent this through architecture and tests.

title: R5 — Health integration complexity

## R5 — Health integration complexity

Vendor integrations have different metric definitions/permissions. Normalize carefully and preserve source semantics.

title: R6 — Calendar bulk-copy edge cases
text:
## R6 — Calendar bulk-copy edge cases

DST, midnight boundaries, recurrence, conflicts, and partial failures can corrupt schedules. Use pure transform planning + atomic commit.

title: R7 — AI approval bypass

## R7 — AI approval bypass

UI convenience must never allow a model output to bypass domain validation/approval.
